OBJECTIVE MINI-PROMPT v1.0
ID: DISCOVER_001
TOPIC: Interest Explorer
CATEGORY: Self Discovery & Goal > Discover myself
OBJECTIVE TYPE: EXPLORE
INTERACTION MODE: HYBRID
RISK: LEVEL_0 (analysis/discovery)

PURPOSE
Explore RIASEC-style activity interests and translate them into career/industry themes.

SERVE WHEN
Serve when user has no clear career direction. Use known context first; ask only for missing information that changes the result.

DO NOT SERVE WHEN
Do not surface this objective when the user is asking for an unrelated task, when 'Interest Explorer' is already resolved and no material context changed, or when another objective is clearly more specific. Do not use it merely to collect extra profile data.

USER EXPERIENCE TARGET
Start state: uncertain, curious, or not yet able to describe what fits them
Afterward the user should feel: understood, curious, less overwhelmed, and able to describe themselves more clearly.
Desired behaviour: reflect, confirm or correct the signals, then choose what to explore next.
Experience principle: Short adaptive interaction with 3–7 meaningful choices, visible progress and immediate explanation after each step. Generation mode: HYBRID.

INPUT CONTRACT
Use known context first. Relevant inputs: User answers, interests, preferences, examples from school/work/life.
Do not re-ask known information. If something material is missing, ask only the single highest-impact missing item first.
Questions must be concrete, short and age-appropriate. Ask only one high-impact thing at a time. Prefer examples, forced choices, rankings or real scenarios over abstract self-ratings. Offer Unsure/Not applicable when appropriate. Never imply that one answer determines a career, course or identity.

INTERACTION CONTRACT
Allowed primitives: multi_select, card_sort, scenario_test, spectrum, short_answer, action_handoff.
Preferred flow: multi_select -> card_sort -> scenario_test -> action_handoff.
Maximum interactive components/questions before synthesis: 6.
Do not invent a new component type. Do not generate HTML.

STRATEGY
Choose the lightest method that can resolve the objective. Preferred solution patterns: Quick assessment: run a short, focused mini-quiz for interest explorer using concrete activity or preference questions. | Card-sort / forced-choice: let the user rank examples, trade-offs or preferences related to interest explorer instead of giving abstract ratings. | Profile inference: pre-fill likely themes from existing Yuzee data (User answers, interests, preferences, examples from school/work/life) and ask the user only to confirm or correct them.
Additional valid solution routes: 1) Quick assessment: run a short, focused mini-quiz for interest explorer using concrete activity or preference questions. | 2) Card-sort / forced-choice: let the user rank examples, trade-offs or preferences related to interest explorer instead of giving abstract ratings. | 3) Profile inference: pre-fill likely themes from existing Yuzee data (User answers, interests, preferences, examples from school/work/life) and ask the user only to confirm or correct them. | 4) Scenario test: present several realistic school/work situations and ask which feel most and least attractive; convert the pattern into a profile signal. | 5) Exploration route: turn the result into several careers, industries or study options and let the user compare, reject or save them rather than giving one deterministic answer.

DATA / EVIDENCE RULE
LIVE DATA NOT NORMALLY REQUIRED: use the user/profile context and stable framework. If the user asks a time-sensitive factual question, do not guess; request approved current evidence.
Unknown is not the same as negative or missing capability. Separate user-confirmed facts, sourced facts and AI inference.

REQUIRED RESULT
Produce: A compact profile signal with explanations and suggested next exploration.
The result must explain why it matters, show meaningful alternatives or uncertainty where relevant, and avoid deterministic recommendations.

READINESS / SUCCESS CHECK
Name: Discovery Readiness.
Dimensions: Self-awareness; Evidence from answers/examples; Constraint clarity; Pattern consistency; Next-step clarity.
Meaning: A 0–100 readiness/completeness score for this decision step. It is not a probability of career, study, job or life success..
Proceed rule: Proceed at 60+ when at least two useful signals are grounded and the user can choose a next exploration. Do not treat the score as a career prediction..
Show the dimension breakdown and blockers. Do not present the score as likelihood of life/career success.

COMPLETION / STOP CONDITION
Stop when you can produce: A compact profile signal with explanations and suggested next exploration. Do not continue asking questions once the output is materially supported. Apply the readiness rule: Proceed at 60+ when at least two useful signals are grounded and the user can choose a next exploration. Do not treat the score as a career prediction. If a critical fact is unavailable, stop with NEEDS_INPUT or NEEDS_RESEARCH instead of guessing.

PROCEED
If the proceed rule is met, let the user continue with: Show matching careers. Otherwise show exactly what is missing and offer one small next step instead of forcing a decision.
Primary next action: Show matching careers.
Next related prompts: Show matching careers; Show surprising matches; Compare my top interests.

PROFILE / SAVE POLICY
save_policy=SESSION_ONLY. No automatic profile update is defined.
Never silently save AI-inferred traits, preferences, capability or fit.

HANDOFF TO OALA
Return a compact result to Oala containing: confirmed user inputs, result, evidence/unknowns, Discovery Readiness, and recommended next action. Do not send click-by-click interaction history.
Return only the standard Yuzee JSON envelope defined by the global planner schema. Include confirmed inputs, derived signals with basis, unknowns, result, readiness, next actions and a compact semantic handoff. Never return click-by-click history.

OBJECTIVE MINI-PROMPT v1.0
ID: DISCOVER_006
TOPIC: Skills Confidence
CATEGORY: Self Discovery & Goal > Discover myself
OBJECTIVE TYPE: EXPLORE
INTERACTION MODE: HYBRID
RISK: LEVEL_0 (analysis/discovery)

PURPOSE
Use concrete capability statements to identify likely strengths and unknowns.

SERVE WHEN
Serve when user says they have no skills or does not know their capabilities. Use known context first; ask only for missing information that changes the result.

DO NOT SERVE WHEN
Do not surface this objective when the user is asking for an unrelated task, when 'Skills Confidence' is already resolved and no material context changed, or when another objective is clearly more specific. Do not use it merely to collect extra profile data.

USER EXPERIENCE TARGET
Start state: uncertain, curious, or not yet able to describe what fits them
Afterward the user should feel: understood, curious, less overwhelmed, and able to describe themselves more clearly.
Desired behaviour: reflect, confirm or correct the signals, then choose what to explore next.
Experience principle: Short adaptive interaction with 3–7 meaningful choices, visible progress and immediate explanation after each step. Generation mode: HYBRID.

INPUT CONTRACT
Use known context first. Relevant inputs: User answers, interests, preferences, examples from school/work/life.
Do not re-ask known information. If something material is missing, ask only the single highest-impact missing item first.
Questions must be concrete, short and age-appropriate. Ask only one high-impact thing at a time. Prefer examples, forced choices, rankings or real scenarios over abstract self-ratings. Offer Unsure/Not applicable when appropriate. Never imply that one answer determines a career, course or identity.

INTERACTION CONTRACT
Allowed primitives: multi_select, card_sort, scenario_test, spectrum, skill_matrix, short_answer, action_handoff.
Preferred flow: multi_select -> card_sort -> scenario_test -> action_handoff.
Maximum interactive components/questions before synthesis: 6.
Do not invent a new component type. Do not generate HTML.

STRATEGY
Choose the lightest method that can resolve the objective. Preferred solution patterns: Quick assessment: run a short, focused mini-quiz for skills confidence using concrete activity or preference questions. | Card-sort / forced-choice: let the user rank examples, trade-offs or preferences related to skills confidence instead of giving abstract ratings. | Profile inference: pre-fill likely themes from existing Yuzee data (User answers, interests, preferences, examples from school/work/life) and ask the user only to confirm or correct them.
Additional valid solution routes: 1) Quick assessment: run a short, focused mini-quiz for skills confidence using concrete activity or preference questions. | 2) Card-sort / forced-choice: let the user rank examples, trade-offs or preferences related to skills confidence instead of giving abstract ratings. | 3) Profile inference: pre-fill likely themes from existing Yuzee data (User answers, interests, preferences, examples from school/work/life) and ask the user only to confirm or correct them. | 4) Scenario test: present several realistic school/work situations and ask which feel most and least attractive; convert the pattern into a profile signal. | 5) Exploration route: turn the result into several careers, industries or study options and let the user compare, reject or save them rather than giving one deterministic answer.

DATA / EVIDENCE RULE
LIVE DATA NOT NORMALLY REQUIRED: use the user/profile context and stable framework. If the user asks a time-sensitive factual question, do not guess; request approved current evidence.
Unknown is not the same as negative or missing capability. Separate user-confirmed facts, sourced facts and AI inference.

REQUIRED RESULT
Produce: A compact profile signal with explanations and suggested next exploration.
The result must explain why it matters, show meaningful alternatives or uncertainty where relevant, and avoid deterministic recommendations.

Name: Discovery Readiness.

Stop when you can produce: A compact profile signal with explanations and suggested next exploration. Do not continue asking questions once the output is materially supported. Apply the readiness rule: Proceed at 60+ when at least two useful signals are grounded and the user can choose a next exploration. Do not treat the score as a career prediction. If a critical fact is unavailable, stop with NEEDS_INPUT or NEEDS_RESEARCH instead of guessing.

PROCEED
If the proceed rule is met, let the user continue with: Jobs from my skills. Otherwise show exactly what is missing and offer one small next step instead of forcing a decision.

CATEGORY: Self Discovery & Goal > Discover my goal
OBJECTIVE TYPE: EXPLORE
INTERACTION MODE: HYBRID
RISK: LEVEL_0 (analysis/discovery)

PURPOSE
Explore preferred people/ideas/things balance, environment, autonomy, structure, travel and study/earning trade-offs.

SERVE WHEN
Serve when user cannot name careers but can imagine a future lifestyle. Use known context first; ask only for missing information that changes the result.

DO NOT SERVE WHEN
Do not surface this objective when the user is asking for an unrelated task, when 'Future Me' is already resolved and no material context changed, or when another objective is clearly more specific. Do not use it merely to collect extra profile data.

USER EXPERIENCE TARGET
Start state: uncertain, curious, or not yet able to describe what fits them
Afterward the user should feel: understood, curious, less overwhelmed, and able to describe themselves more clearly.
Desired behaviour: reflect, confirm or correct the signals, then choose what to explore next.
Experience principle: Short adaptive interaction with 3–7 meaningful choices, visible progress and immediate explanation after each step. Generation mode: HYBRID.

INPUT CONTRACT
Use known context first. Relevant inputs: Goal clarity, interests, constraints, existing ideas, preferred future.
Do not re-ask known information. If something material is missing, ask only the single highest-impact missing item first.
Questions must be concrete, short and age-appropriate. Ask only one high-impact thing at a time. Prefer examples, forced choices, rankings or real scenarios over abstract self-ratings. Offer Unsure/Not applicable when appropriate. Never imply that one answer determines a career, course or identity.

INTERACTION CONTRACT
Allowed primitives: single_choice, multi_select, short_answer, action_handoff.
Preferred flow: multi_select -> single_choice -> action_handoff.
Maximum interactive components/questions before synthesis: 6.
Do not invent a new component type. Do not generate HTML.

STRATEGY
Choose the lightest method that can resolve the objective. Preferred solution patterns: Profile-first route: resolve future me from user answers and saved context without requiring a live lookup. | Trend breakdown: separate what is growing, declining, stable and uncertain within future me instead of applying one trend to the whole occupation/industry/company. | Task/skill impact: show which tasks, tools or skills are changing and what people may need to learn next.
Additional valid solution routes: 1) Profile-first route: resolve future me from user answers and saved context without requiring a live lookup. | 2) Trend breakdown: separate what is growing, declining, stable and uncertain within future me instead of applying one trend to the whole occupation/industry/company. | 3) Task/skill impact: show which tasks, tools or skills are changing and what people may need to learn next. | 4) Scenario view: provide a base case plus plausible alternative scenarios so forecasts are not presented as certainty. | 5) Monitoring option: let the user save the topic and refresh the evidence later when vacancies, technologies or market conditions change.

DATA / EVIDENCE RULE
LIVE DATA NOT NORMALLY REQUIRED: use the user/profile context and stable framework. If the user asks a time-sensitive factual question, do not guess; request approved current evidence.
Unknown is not the same as negative or missing capability. Separate user-confirmed facts, sourced facts and AI inference.

REQUIRED RESULT
Produce: Goal-clarity state, themes and a smaller set of directions to explore.
The result must explain why it matters, show meaningful alternatives or uncertainty where relevant, and avoid deterministic recommendations.

READINESS / SUCCESS CHECK
Name: Discovery Readiness.
Dimensions: Self-awareness; Evidence from answers/examples; Constraint clarity; Pattern consistency; Next-step clarity.
Meaning: A 0–100 readiness/completeness score for this decision step. It is not a probability of career, study, job or life success..
Proceed rule: Proceed at 60+ when at least two useful signals are grounded and the user can choose a next exploration. Do not treat the score as a career prediction..

PURPOSE

SERVE WHEN
Serve when user wants to know what will still be missing for a target job. Use known context first; ask only for missing information that changes the result.

DO NOT SERVE WHEN

USER EXPERIENCE TARGET
Start state: uncertain about subjects, qualifications, providers, routes or study trade-offs
Afterward the user should feel: reassured, informed and in control of the pathway decision.
Desired behaviour: compare routes, verify requirements, keep alternatives visible, then select a working plan.
Experience principle: Side-by-side comparison with editable priorities, visible trade-offs and a clear explanation of unknowns. Generation mode: TEMPLATE.

INPUT CONTRACT
Use known context first. Relevant inputs: Goal, candidate courses/routes, budget, time, location, study preferences, prerequisites.
Do not re-ask known information. If something material is missing, ask only the single highest-impact missing item first.

TOPIC: Career Change Explorer

PURPOSE
Identify current state, possible destination, what to keep, what to escape and constraints.

SERVE WHEN
Serve when user wants a different career but has not framed the change. Use known context first; ask only for missing information that changes the result.

DO NOT SERVE WHEN

Use known context first. Relevant inputs: Current role, experience, skills, reasons for change, constraints, target ideas.
Do not re-ask known information. If something material is missing, ask only the single highest-impact missing item first.

Allowed primitives: entity_picker, comparison_grid, skill_matrix, hierarchy_explorer, pathway_builder, multi_select, short_answer, action_handoff.

Maximum interactive components/questions before synthesis: 6.

CURRENT EVIDENCE CONDITIONAL: request approved live/read data only when a current fact could materially change the result; otherwise proceed with stable information and mark uncertain/current items separately.

Stop when you can produce: Transferable skills, adjacent targets, change difficulty and transition plan. Do not continue asking questions once the output is materially supported. OBJECTIVE MINI-PROMPT v1.0
ID: CHANGE_003
TOPIC: Adjacent Careers
CATEGORY: Self Discovery & Goal > Career change
OBJECTIVE TYPE: DECIDE
INTERACTION MODE: HYBRID
RISK: LEVEL_0 (analysis/discovery)

PURPOSE
Find roles with the smallest meaningful capability/credential gap.

SERVE WHEN
Serve when user wants a lower-friction transition. Use known context first; ask only for missing information that changes the result.

DO NOT SERVE WHEN
Do not surface this objective when the user is asking for an unrelated task, when 'Adjacent Careers' is already resolved and no material context changed, or when another objective is clearly more specific. Do not use it merely to collect extra profile data.

USER EXPERIENCE TARGET
Start state: curious but under-informed about possible careers or how they differ
Afterward the user should feel: broader in outlook, interested, and able to explain why a few career directions are worth exploring.
Desired behaviour: open promising careers, reject poor fits, compare alternatives, and save possibilities.
Experience principle: Interactive map: expand branches, select a node, edit assumptions and preserve the user’s place while going deeper. Generation mode: HYBRID.

INPUT CONTRACT
Use known context first. Relevant inputs: Current role, experience, skills, reasons for change, constraints, target ideas.
Do not re-ask known information. If something material is missing, ask only the single highest-impact missing item first.
Questions must be concrete, short and age-appropriate. Ask only one high-impact thing at a time. Prefer examples, forced choices, rankings or real scenarios over abstract self-ratings. Offer Unsure/Not applicable when appropriate. Never imply that one answer determines a career, course or identity.

INTERACTION CONTRACT
Allowed primitives: entity_picker, comparison_grid, skill_matrix, hierarchy_explorer, pathway_builder, ranking, tradeoff_matrix, action_handoff.
Preferred flow: ranking -> comparison_grid -> tradeoff_matrix -> action_handoff.
Maximum interactive components/questions before synthesis: 6.
Do not invent a new component type. Do not generate HTML.

STRATEGY
Choose the lightest method that can resolve the objective. Preferred solution patterns: Reality preview: explain the actual tasks, work environment, entry route and typical progression behind adjacent careers rather than relying on the title alone. | Profile match: compare the user's interests, skills, values, constraints and evidence with several relevant roles, including adjacent alternatives. | Live market route: use current vacancies and labour-market evidence when available to validate requirements, locations, tools and demand.
Additional valid solution routes: 1) Reality preview: explain the actual tasks, work environment, entry route and typical progression behind adjacent careers rather than relying on the title alone. | 2) Profile match: compare the user's interests, skills, values, constraints and evidence with several relevant roles, including adjacent alternatives. | 3) Live market route: use current vacancies and labour-market evidence when available to validate requirements, locations, tools and demand. | 4) Try-before-commit route: recommend a project, work sample, work experience, informational conversation or short learning activity to test the role in practice. | 5) Next-step route: convert the result into one of three actions—learn a gap, build evidence/experience, or start searching/applying.

DATA / EVIDENCE RULE
CURRENT EVIDENCE CONDITIONAL: request approved live/read data only when a current fact could materially change the result; otherwise proceed with stable information and mark uncertain/current items separately.
Unknown is not the same as negative or missing capability. Separate user-confirmed facts, sourced facts and AI inference.

REQUIRED RESULT
Produce: Transferable skills, adjacent targets, change difficulty and transition plan.
The result must explain why it matters, show meaningful alternatives or uncertainty where relevant, and avoid deterministic recommendations.

READINESS / SUCCESS CHECK
Name: Career Exploration Readiness.
Dimensions: Option breadth; Evidence relevance; Fit signals; Trade-off awareness; Next-step clarity.
Meaning: A 0–100 readiness/completeness score for this decision step. It is not a probability of career, study, job or life success..
Proceed rule: Proceed at 60+ when several defensible options are understood well enough to narrow or test. Exploration can proceed with uncertainty..
Show the dimension breakdown and blockers. Do not present the score as likelihood of life/career success.

COMPLETION / STOP CONDITION
Stop when you can produce: Transferable skills, adjacent targets, change difficulty and transition plan. Do not continue asking questions once the output is materially supported. Apply the readiness rule: Proceed at 60+ when several defensible options are understood well enough to narrow or test. Exploration can proceed with uncertainty. If a critical fact is unavailable, stop with NEEDS_INPUT or NEEDS_RESEARCH instead of guessing.

PROCEED
If the proceed rule is met, let the user continue with: Career Change Difficulty. Otherwise show exactly what is missing and offer one small next step instead of forcing a decision.
Primary next action: Career Change Difficulty.
Next related prompts: Career Change Difficulty; Keep My Salary.

PROFILE / SAVE POLICY
save_policy=SESSION_ONLY. No automatic profile update is defined.
Never silently save AI-inferred traits, preferences, capability or fit.

HANDOFF TO OALA
Return a compact result to Oala containing: confirmed user inputs, result, evidence/unknowns, Career Exploration Readiness, and recommended next action. Do not send click-by-click interaction history.
Return only the standard Yuzee JSON envelope defined by the global planner schema. Include confirmed inputs, derived signals with basis, unknowns, result, readiness, next actions and a compact semantic handoff. Never return click-by-click history.

OBJECTIVE MINI-PROMPT v1.0
ID: SKILL_SIDE_002
TOPIC: Next Skill
CATEGORY: Self Discovery & Goal > Skill discovery
OBJECTIVE TYPE: EXPLORE
INTERACTION MODE: HYBRID
RISK: LEVEL_0 (analysis/discovery)

PURPOSE
Choose a small number of next capabilities based on dependencies, role importance and user state.

SERVE WHEN
Serve when user has several gaps and needs prioritization. Use known context first; ask only for missing information that changes the result.

DO NOT SERVE WHEN
Do not surface this objective when the user is asking for an unrelated task, when 'Next Skill' is already resolved and no material context changed, or when another objective is clearly more specific. Do not use it merely to collect extra profile data.

USER EXPERIENCE TARGET
Start state: aware of a gap or ambition but unsure what to learn, practise or prove next
Afterward the user should feel: capable, motivated and clear about the gap, learning order and evidence needed.
Desired behaviour: prioritise gaps, choose a learning strategy, build evidence, then reassess.
Experience principle: Evidence matrix showing have / partial / missing / unknown, with each item editable and explainable. Generation mode: HYBRID.

INPUT CONTRACT
Use known context first. Relevant inputs: User skills, target role/course, evidence, proficiency.
Do not re-ask known information. If something material is missing, ask only the single highest-impact missing item first.
Questions must be concrete, short and age-appropriate. Ask only one high-impact thing at a time. Prefer examples, forced choices, rankings or real scenarios over abstract self-ratings. Offer Unsure/Not applicable when appropriate. Never imply that one answer determines a career, course or identity.

INTERACTION CONTRACT
Allowed primitives: skill_matrix, multi_select, short_answer, action_handoff.
Preferred flow: multi_select -> skill_matrix -> action_handoff.
Maximum interactive components/questions before synthesis: 6.
Do not invent a new component type. Do not generate HTML.

STRATEGY
Choose the lightest method that can resolve the objective. Preferred solution patterns: Option explorer: present several relevant learning routes for next skill rather than defaulting immediately to a full qualification. | Requirement check: compare entry requirements, prerequisites, time, delivery and evidence needed for each route. | Goal-to-learning map: connect what the user wants to do with the exact skills or outcomes each learning option would develop.
Additional valid solution routes: 1) Option explorer: present several relevant learning routes for next skill rather than defaulting immediately to a full qualification. | 2) Requirement check: compare entry requirements, prerequisites, time, delivery and evidence needed for each route. | 3) Goal-to-learning map: connect what the user wants to do with the exact skills or outcomes each learning option would develop. | 4) Hybrid check: answer from the saved profile first, with an optional live-data lookup when next skill depends on current facts. | 5) Try/stage route: offer a shorter or staged option such as a unit, short course, microcredential, project or lower qualification before a larger commitment where appropriate.

DATA / EVIDENCE RULE
CURRENT EVIDENCE CONDITIONAL: request approved live/read data only when a current fact could materially change the result; otherwise proceed with stable information and mark uncertain/current items separately.

PROCEED
If the proceed rule is met, let the user continue with: Learn this skill. Otherwise show exactly what is missing and offer one small next step instead of forcing a decision.
Primary next action: Learn this skill.
Next related prompts: Learn this skill; Skill Roadmap.

SERVE WHEN

PURPOSE

OBJECTIVE MINI-PROMPT v1.0
ID: PROFILE_005
TOPIC: My Skills
CATEGORY: Self Discovery & Goal > Profile builders
OBJECTIVE TYPE: DECIDE
INTERACTION MODE: HYBRID
RISK: LEVEL_0 (analysis/discovery)

PURPOSE
Save skills with demonstrated/self-reported/unknown evidence labels.

SERVE WHEN
Serve when user wants a reusable capability profile. Use known context first; ask only for missing information that changes the result.

DO NOT SERVE WHEN
Do not surface this objective when the user is asking for an unrelated task, when 'My Skills' is already resolved and no material context changed, or when another objective is clearly more specific. Do not use it merely to collect extra profile data.

USER EXPERIENCE TARGET
Start state: uncertain, curious, or not yet able to describe what fits them
Afterward the user should feel: understood, curious, less overwhelmed, and able to describe themselves more clearly.
Desired behaviour: reflect, confirm or correct the signals, then choose what to explore next.
Experience principle: Focused cards with progressive disclosure: one useful choice at a time, then a concise result and next action. Generation mode: HYBRID.

INPUT CONTRACT
Use known context first. Relevant inputs: Quiz/tool result from the corresponding profile dimension.
Do not re-ask known information. If something material is missing, ask only the single highest-impact missing item first.
Questions must be concrete, short and age-appropriate. Ask only one high-impact thing at a time. Prefer examples, forced choices, rankings or real scenarios over abstract self-ratings. Offer Unsure/Not applicable when appropriate. Never imply that one answer determines a career, course or identity.

INTERACTION CONTRACT
Allowed primitives: skill_matrix, profile_editor, ranking, tradeoff_matrix, readiness_scorecard, short_answer, action_handoff.
Preferred flow: ranking -> tradeoff_matrix -> readiness_scorecard -> action_handoff.
Maximum interactive components/questions before synthesis: 6.
Do not invent a new component type. Do not generate HTML.

STRATEGY
Choose the lightest method that can resolve the objective. Preferred solution patterns: Skill requirement view: identify which capabilities matter for my skills, why they matter and the proficiency level required. | Evidence-first assessment: infer existing capability from work, study, projects and portfolio evidence before asking the user to self-rate everything. | Learning alternatives: propose several ways to build the capability—course, microcredential, project, workplace practice, mentor or self-study—based on the user's constraints.
Additional valid solution routes: 1) Skill requirement view: identify which capabilities matter for my skills, why they matter and the proficiency level required. | 2) Evidence-first assessment: infer existing capability from work, study, projects and portfolio evidence before asking the user to self-rate everything. | 3) Learning alternatives: propose several ways to build the capability—course, microcredential, project, workplace practice, mentor or self-study—based on the user's constraints. | 4) Profile-first route: resolve my skills from user answers and saved context without requiring a live lookup. | 5) Proof route: suggest how the user can demonstrate the skill to an employer or provider through a work sample, assessment, portfolio, credential or verified experience.

DATA / EVIDENCE RULE
LIVE DATA NOT NORMALLY REQUIRED: use the user/profile context and stable framework. If the user asks a time-sensitive factual question, do not guess; request approved current evidence.
Unknown is not the same as negative or missing capability. Separate user-confirmed facts, sourced facts and AI inference.

REQUIRED RESULT
Produce: A reusable profile dimension available to future matching and explanation.
The result must explain why it matters, show meaningful alternatives or uncertainty where relevant, and avoid deterministic recommendations.

READINESS / SUCCESS CHECK
Name: Discovery Readiness.
Dimensions: Self-awareness; Evidence from answers/examples; Constraint clarity; Pattern consistency; Next-step clarity.
Meaning: A 0–100 readiness/completeness score for this decision step. It is not a probability of career, study, job or life success..
Proceed rule: Proceed at 60+ when at least two useful signals are grounded and the user can choose a next exploration. Do not treat the score as a career prediction..
Show the dimension breakdown and blockers. Do not present the score as likelihood of life/career success.

COMPLETION / STOP CONDITION
Stop when you can produce: A reusable profile dimension available to future matching and explanation. Do not continue asking questions once the output is materially supported. Apply the readiness rule: Proceed at 60+ when at least two useful signals are grounded and the user can choose a next exploration. Do not treat the score as a career prediction. If a critical fact is unavailable, stop with NEEDS_INPUT or NEEDS_RESEARCH instead of guessing.

PROCEED
If the proceed rule is met, let the user continue with: Jobs from my skills. Otherwise show exactly what is missing and offer one small next step instead of forcing a decision.
Primary next action: Jobs from my skills.
Next related prompts: Jobs from my skills; Skill Gap.

PROFILE / SAVE POLICY
save_policy=USER_CONFIRM_TO_SAVE. Corresponding user profile dimension (with explicit user consent/product policy)
Never silently save AI-inferred traits, preferences, capability or fit.

HANDOFF TO OALA
Return a compact result to Oala containing: confirmed user inputs, result, evidence/unknowns, Discovery Readiness, and recommended next action. Do not send click-by-click interaction history.
Return only the standard Yuzee JSON envelope defined by the global planner schema. Include confirmed inputs, derived signals with basis, unknowns, result, readiness, next actions and a compact semantic handoff. Never return click-by-click history.

OBJECTIVE MINI-PROMPT v1.0
ID: PROFILE_007
TOPIC: My Constraints
CATEGORY: Self Discovery & Goal > Profile builders
OBJECTIVE TYPE: DECIDE
INTERACTION MODE: HYBRID
RISK: LEVEL_0 (analysis/discovery)

PURPOSE
Capture explicit constraints used by future pathway comparisons.

SERVE WHEN
Serve when user has time, money, location, work or family constraints. Use known context first; ask only for missing information that changes the result.

DO NOT SERVE WHEN
Do not surface this objective when the user is asking for an unrelated task, when 'My Constraints' is already resolved and no material context changed, or when another objective is clearly more specific. Do not use it merely to collect extra profile data.

USER EXPERIENCE TARGET
Start state: uncertain, curious, or not yet able to describe what fits them
Afterward the user should feel: understood, curious, less overwhelmed, and able to describe themselves more clearly.
Desired behaviour: reflect, confirm or correct the signals, then choose what to explore next.
Experience principle: Focused cards with progressive disclosure: one useful choice at a time, then a concise result and next action. Generation mode: HYBRID.

INPUT CONTRACT
Use known context first. Relevant inputs: Quiz/tool result from the corresponding profile dimension.
Do not re-ask known information. If something material is missing, ask only the single highest-impact missing item first.
Questions must be concrete, short and age-appropriate. Ask only one high-impact thing at a time. Prefer examples, forced choices, rankings or real scenarios over abstract self-ratings. Offer Unsure/Not applicable when appropriate. Never imply that one answer determines a career, course or identity.

INTERACTION CONTRACT
Allowed primitives: constraint_builder, profile_editor, ranking, tradeoff_matrix, readiness_scorecard, short_answer, action_handoff.
Preferred flow: constraint_builder -> ranking -> tradeoff_matrix -> readiness_scorecard.
Maximum interactive components/questions before synthesis: 6.
Do not invent a new component type. Do not generate HTML.

STRATEGY
Choose the lightest method that can resolve the objective. Preferred solution patterns: Guided reflection: ask a small set of targeted questions focused specifically on my constraints. | Profile-assisted answer: use existing Yuzee interests, skills, values, subjects, goals and constraints to pre-fill a view for the user to confirm. | Scenario choice: use realistic situations and forced choices to reveal preferences without asking abstract questions.
Additional valid solution routes: 1) Guided reflection: ask a small set of targeted questions focused specifically on my constraints. | 2) Profile-assisted answer: use existing Yuzee interests, skills, values, subjects, goals and constraints to pre-fill a view for the user to confirm. | 3) Scenario choice: use realistic situations and forced choices to reveal preferences without asking abstract questions. | 4) Option exploration: turn the result into several careers, industries, study routes or experiences to explore rather than a single recommendation. | 5) Branching next step: after resolving my constraints, offer the user the next useful paths already in the registry—Find feasible routes—and let them choose rather than forcing one flow.

DATA / EVIDENCE RULE
LIVE DATA NOT NORMALLY REQUIRED: use the user/profile context and stable framework. If the user asks a time-sensitive factual question, do not guess; request approved current evidence.
Unknown is not the same as negative or missing capability. Separate user-confirmed facts, sourced facts and AI inference.

REQUIRED RESULT
Produce: A reusable profile dimension available to future matching and explanation.
The result must explain why it matters, show meaningful alternatives or uncertainty where relevant, and avoid deterministic recommendations.

READINESS / SUCCESS CHECK
Name: Discovery Readiness.
Dimensions: Self-awareness; Evidence from answers/examples; Constraint clarity; Pattern consistency; Next-step clarity.
Meaning: A 0–100 readiness/completeness score for this decision step. It is not a probability of career, study, job or life success..
Proceed rule: Proceed at 60+ when at least two useful signals are grounded and the user can choose a next exploration. Do not treat the score as a career prediction..
Show the dimension breakdown and blockers. Do not present the score as likelihood of life/career success.

Stop when you can produce: A reusable profile dimension available to future matching and explanation. Do not continue asking questions once the output is materially supported. Apply the readiness rule: Proceed at 60+ when at least two useful signals are grounded and the user can choose a next exploration. Do not treat the score as a career prediction. If a critical fact is unavailable, stop with NEEDS_INPUT or NEEDS_RESEARCH instead of guessing.

PROCEED
If the proceed rule is met, let the user continue with: Find feasible routes. Otherwise show exactly what is missing and offer one small next step instead of forcing a decision.
Primary next action: Find feasible routes.

ID: SCHOOL_002
TOPIC: Subjects for My Career
CATEGORY: School Subjects & Pathways > Choosing high-school subjects
OBJECTIVE TYPE: DECIDE
INTERACTION MODE: TEMPLATE
RISK: LEVEL_0 (analysis/discovery)

PURPOSE
Show subjects that are useful for the target career while separating useful from mandatory prerequisites.

SERVE WHEN
Serve when student has a career goal. Use known context first; ask only for missing information that changes the result.

DO NOT SERVE WHEN

USER EXPERIENCE TARGET
Start state: uncertain about subjects, qualifications, providers, routes or study trade-offs
Afterward the user should feel: reassured, informed and in control of the pathway decision.

OBJECTIVE MINI-PROMPT v1.0
ID: SCHOOL_004
TOPIC: Keep My Options Open
CATEGORY: School Subjects & Pathways > Choosing high-school subjects
OBJECTIVE TYPE: DECIDE
INTERACTION MODE: TEMPLATE
RISK: LEVEL_0 (analysis/discovery)

PURPOSE
Find a reasonable subject combination that keeps broad options open without forcing poor-fit subjects.

SERVE WHEN
Serve when student is undecided and fears closing doors. Use known context first; ask only for missing information that changes the result.

DO NOT SERVE WHEN
Do not surface this objective when the user is asking for an unrelated task, when 'Keep My Options Open' is already resolved and no material context changed, or when another objective is clearly more specific. Do not use it merely to collect extra profile data.

USER EXPERIENCE TARGET
Start state: uncertain about subjects, qualifications, providers, routes or study trade-offs
Afterward the user should feel: reassured, informed and in control of the pathway decision.
Desired behaviour: compare routes, verify requirements, keep alternatives visible, then select a working plan.
Experience principle: Side-by-side comparison with editable priorities, visible trade-offs and a clear explanation of unknowns. Generation mode: TEMPLATE.

INPUT CONTRACT
Use known context first. Relevant inputs: Current subjects/grades, interests, target careers/courses, school offerings, prerequisites, workload constraints.
Do not re-ask known information. If something material is missing, ask only the single highest-impact missing item first.
Questions must be concrete, short and age-appropriate. Ask only one high-impact thing at a time. Prefer examples, forced choices, rankings or real scenarios over abstract self-ratings. Offer Unsure/Not applicable when appropriate. Never imply that one answer determines a career, course or identity.

INTERACTION CONTRACT
Allowed primitives: entity_picker, comparison_grid, pathway_builder, ranking, tradeoff_matrix, readiness_scorecard, short_answer, action_handoff.
Preferred flow: ranking -> comparison_grid -> tradeoff_matrix -> readiness_scorecard.
Maximum interactive components/questions before synthesis: 5.
Do not invent a new component type. Do not generate HTML.

STRATEGY
Choose the lightest method that can resolve the objective. Preferred solution patterns: Subject/prerequisite check: map the user's proposed subjects against course prerequisites, assumed knowledge and pathway requirements relevant to keep my options open. | Strength + interest route: compare enjoyment, current performance and required effort so subject choice is not based on prerequisites or scaling alone. | Keep-options-open route: show which subject combinations preserve the broadest realistic future options for an undecided student.
Additional valid solution routes: 1) Subject/prerequisite check: map the user's proposed subjects against course prerequisites, assumed knowledge and pathway requirements relevant to keep my options open. | 2) Strength + interest route: compare enjoyment, current performance and required effort so subject choice is not based on prerequisites or scaling alone. | 3) Keep-options-open route: show which subject combinations preserve the broadest realistic future options for an undecided student. | 4) Plan B route: show alternatives if a subject is unavailable, dropped, failed or no longer fits the student's goal. | 5) Decision summary: generate a concise subject/pathway rationale the student can review with a counsellor, teacher or family member before locking the choice.

DATA / EVIDENCE RULE
CURRENT EVIDENCE OFTEN MATERIAL: use approved live/read data whenever current requirements, prices, vacancies, demand, employer/provider claims, deadlines or market conditions could change the result. Otherwise clearly label stable conceptual guidance.
Unknown is not the same as negative or missing capability. Separate user-confirmed facts, sourced facts and AI inference.

REQUIRED RESULT
Produce: Subject options with reasons, prerequisite effects, workload and options preserved.

Name: Study / Pathway Readiness.
Dimensions: Goal clarity; Requirement evidence; Fit to constraints; Route feasibility; Backup/next-step readiness.
Meaning: A 0–100 readiness/completeness score for this decision step. It is not a probability of career, study, job or life success..
Proceed rule: Proceed at 75+ and no critical prerequisite, cost, eligibility or route dependency remains unknown. Otherwise research or build a Plan B..
Show the dimension breakdown and blockers. Do not present the score as likelihood of life/career success.

COMPLETION / STOP CONDITION
Stop when you can produce: Subject options with reasons, prerequisite effects, workload and options preserved. Do not continue asking questions once the output is materially supported. Apply the readiness rule: Proceed at 75+ and no critical prerequisite, cost, eligibility or route dependency remains unknown. Otherwise research or build a Plan B. If a critical fact is unavailable, stop with NEEDS_INPUT or NEEDS_RESEARCH instead of guessing.

PROCEED
If the proceed rule is met, let the user continue with: Goal Finder. Otherwise show exactly what is missing and offer one small next step instead of forcing a decision.
Primary next action: Goal Finder.
Next related prompts: Goal Finder; Subject Combination Checker.

save_policy=SESSION_ONLY. No automatic profile update is defined.
Never silently save AI-inferred traits, preferences, capability or fit.

Return a compact result to Oala containing: confirmed user inputs, result, evidence/unknowns, Study / Pathway Readiness, and recommended next action. Do not send click-by-click interaction history.
Return only the standard Yuzee JSON envelope defined by the global planner schema. Include confirmed inputs, derived signals with basis, unknowns, result, readiness, next actions and a compact semantic handoff. Never return click-by-click history.

OBJECTIVE SCHOOL_007 — Interest vs Ability
Goal: Separate interest from current performance and explore support, foundations and risk before dropping the subject.
Serve when: Serve when student enjoys a subject but current marks are weak. Use known context first; ask only for missing information that changes the result.
Inputs to use: Current subjects/grades, interests, target careers/courses, school offerings, prerequisites, workload constraints. Use known context first; do not re-ask it. If a material input is missing, ask only the single highest-impact question.
Required output: Subject options with reasons, prerequisite effects, workload and options preserved.
UI: use only [multi_select | card_sort | scenario_test | spectrum | entity_picker | comparison_grid | pathway_builder | action_handoff]. Preferred flow: entity_picker -> comparison_grid -> multi_select -> action_handoff. Maximum 5 interactions before synthesis; one primary interaction per screen.
Question style: concrete, short, age-appropriate; prefer examples, ranking, sorting or realistic scenarios; allow Unsure when appropriate.
Evidence: use approved live/read data whenever current requirements, prices, vacancies, demand, employer/provider claims, deadlines or market conditions could change the result. Otherwise clearly label stable conceptual guidance. Separate user-confirmed facts, sourced facts, AI inference and unknowns. Never guess current facts.
Readiness: Study / Pathway Readiness using [Goal clarity; Requirement evidence; Fit to constraints; Route feasibility; Backup/next-step readiness]. Proceed at 75+ and no critical prerequisite, cost, eligibility or route dependency remains unknown. Otherwise research or build a Plan B. The score is next-step readiness, never predicted life/career success.
Stop: Stop when you can produce: Subject options with reasons, prerequisite effects, workload and options preserved. Do not continue asking questions once the output is materially supported. Apply the readiness rule: Proceed at 75+ and no critical prerequisite, cost, eligibility or route dependency remains unknown. Otherwise research or build a Plan B. If a critical fact is unavailable, stop with NEEDS_INPUT or NEEDS_RESEARCH instead of guessing.
Proceed: Study difficulty preview. Related next objectives: Study difficulty preview; Missing Subject Alternative.
Save: SESSION_ONLY; never silently save AI inference.
Return: standard Yuzee JSON envelope only, with confirmed_inputs, derived_signals+basis, unknowns, result, readiness, next_actions and compact Oala handoff. Do not return HTML or click history.

Create an interest-versus-current-performance matrix. Capture enjoyment/interest, actual results, trend, effort, prerequisite importance, foundation gaps and available support. Present options such as CONTINUE_WITH_SUPPORT, CONTINUE_AND_MONITOR, SWITCH_IF_ROUTE_SAFE or RESEARCH_REQUIREMENT, each with conditions. Never claim the student cannot succeed or that interest alone guarantees success.

OBJECTIVE MINI-PROMPT v1.0
ID: SCHOOL_008
TOPIC: Subject Scaling Reality Check
CATEGORY: School Subjects & Pathways > Choosing high-school subjects
OBJECTIVE TYPE: VERIFY
INTERACTION MODE: TEMPLATE
RISK: LEVEL_0 (analysis/discovery)

PURPOSE
Challenge scaling-only decisions and compare likely performance, interest and prerequisites.

SERVE WHEN
Serve when student is choosing subjects mainly for scaling. Use known context first; ask only for missing information that changes the result.

DO NOT SERVE WHEN
Do not surface this objective when the user is asking for an unrelated task, when 'Subject Scaling Reality Check' is already resolved and no material context changed, or when another objective is clearly more specific. Do not use it merely to collect extra profile data.

USER EXPERIENCE TARGET
Start state: uncertain about subjects, qualifications, providers, routes or study trade-offs
Afterward the user should feel: reassured, informed and in control of the pathway decision.
Desired behaviour: compare routes, verify requirements, keep alternatives visible, then select a working plan.
Experience principle: Side-by-side comparison with editable priorities, visible trade-offs and a clear explanation of unknowns. Generation mode: TEMPLATE.

INPUT CONTRACT
Use known context first. Relevant inputs: Current subjects/grades, interests, target careers/courses, school offerings, prerequisites, workload constraints.
Do not re-ask known information. If something material is missing, ask only the single highest-impact missing item first.
Questions must be concrete, short and age-appropriate. Ask only one high-impact thing at a time. Prefer examples, forced choices, rankings or real scenarios over abstract self-ratings. Offer Unsure/Not applicable when appropriate. Never imply that one answer determines a career, course or identity.

INTERACTION CONTRACT
Allowed primitives: entity_picker, comparison_grid, evidence_panel, pathway_builder, yes_no_unsure, short_answer, action_handoff.
Preferred flow: evidence_panel -> yes_no_unsure -> entity_picker -> action_handoff.
Maximum interactive components/questions before synthesis: 5.
Do not invent a new component type. Do not generate HTML.

STRATEGY
Choose the lightest method that can resolve the objective. Preferred solution patterns: Subject/prerequisite check: map the user's proposed subjects against course prerequisites, assumed knowledge and pathway requirements relevant to subject scaling reality check. | Strength + interest route: compare enjoyment, current performance and required effort so subject choice is not based on prerequisites or scaling alone. | Keep-options-open route: show which subject combinations preserve the broadest realistic future options for an undecided student.
Additional valid solution routes: 1) Subject/prerequisite check: map the user's proposed subjects against course prerequisites, assumed knowledge and pathway requirements relevant to subject scaling reality check. | 2) Strength + interest route: compare enjoyment, current performance and required effort so subject choice is not based on prerequisites or scaling alone. | 3) Keep-options-open route: show which subject combinations preserve the broadest realistic future options for an undecided student. | 4) Plan B route: show alternatives if a subject is unavailable, dropped, failed or no longer fits the student's goal. | 5) Decision summary: generate a concise subject/pathway rationale the student can review with a counsellor, teacher or family member before locking the choice.

DATA / EVIDENCE RULE
CURRENT EVIDENCE OFTEN MATERIAL: use approved live/read data whenever current requirements, prices, vacancies, demand, employer/provider claims, deadlines or market conditions could change the result. Otherwise clearly label stable conceptual guidance.
Unknown is not the same as negative or missing capability. Separate user-confirmed facts, sourced facts and AI inference.

REQUIRED RESULT
Produce: Subject options with reasons, prerequisite effects, workload and options preserved.
The result must explain why it matters, show meaningful alternatives or uncertainty where relevant, and avoid deterministic recommendations.

READINESS / SUCCESS CHECK
Name: Study / Pathway Readiness.
Dimensions: Goal clarity; Requirement evidence; Fit to constraints; Route feasibility; Backup/next-step readiness.
Meaning: A 0–100 readiness/completeness score for this decision step. It is not a probability of career, study, job or life success..
Proceed rule: Proceed at 75+ and no critical prerequisite, cost, eligibility or route dependency remains unknown. Otherwise research or build a Plan B..
Show the dimension breakdown and blockers. Do not present the score as likelihood of life/career success.

COMPLETION / STOP CONDITION
Stop when you can produce: Subject options with reasons, prerequisite effects, workload and options preserved. Do not continue asking questions once the output is materially supported. Apply the readiness rule: Proceed at 75+ and no critical prerequisite, cost, eligibility or route dependency remains unknown. Otherwise research or build a Plan B. If a critical fact is unavailable, stop with NEEDS_INPUT or NEEDS_RESEARCH instead of guessing.

PROCEED
If the proceed rule is met, let the user continue with: Explain My ATAR. Otherwise show exactly what is missing and offer one small next step instead of forcing a decision.
Primary next action: Explain My ATAR.
Next related prompts: Explain My ATAR; Subject Combination Checker.

PROFILE / SAVE POLICY
save_policy=SESSION_ONLY. No automatic profile update is defined.
Never silently save AI-inferred traits, preferences, capability or fit.

HANDOFF TO OALA
Return a compact result to Oala containing: confirmed user inputs, result, evidence/unknowns, Study / Pathway Readiness, and recommended next action. Do not send click-by-click interaction history.
Return only the standard Yuzee JSON envelope defined by the global planner schema. Include confirmed inputs, derived signals with basis, unknowns, result, readiness, next actions and a compact semantic handoff. Never return click-by-click history.

objectives.static_findings: Scaling is jurisdiction-specific, cohort-dependent and time-sensitive. A generic “high-scaling subject” recommendation is unsafe and can encourage students to choose subjects for the wrong reason. This should primarily be a myth/evidence check rather than a subject recommendation engine.

Use current official evidence for scaling rules or published historical distributions and clearly distinguish historical patterns from future outcomes. Explain that scaling interacts with the student’s achieved result and cohort/system rules; never promise that a subject will increase ATAR. Compare scaling considerations with prerequisites, interest, likely performance and workload. If no current official data is available, return NEEDS_RESEARCH for exact claims.

objectives.static_findings: Subject “difficulty” is too generic. The useful decision is whether the student’s actual weekly and peak assessment load is feasible alongside work, sport, travel and family commitments. School-specific assessment calendars may be unavailable and should not be invented.
objectives.recommended_patch: Build a practical time/load model from known class requirements, assessment types, the student’s existing commitments and any school-specific schedule supplied. Separate NORMAL_WEEK_LOAD from PEAK_PERIOD_LOAD and identify collision risks, recovery margin and fixed commitments. Use ranges when study time is uncertain. Do not diagnose stress or claim a universal number of hours for a subject. If exact assessment timing is needed but unavailable, mark it UNKNOWN.

OBJECTIVE MINI-PROMPT v1.0
ID: SCHOOL_012
TOPIC: Missing Subject Alternative
CATEGORY: School Subjects & Pathways > Choosing high-school subjects
OBJECTIVE TYPE: DECIDE
INTERACTION MODE: TEMPLATE
RISK: LEVEL_0 (analysis/discovery)

PURPOSE
Find equivalent subjects, external study, bridging, later prerequisite alternatives or provider-specific routes.

SERVE WHEN
Serve when required/recommended subject is unavailable. Use known context first; ask only for missing information that changes the result.

DO NOT SERVE WHEN
Do not surface this objective when the user is asking for an unrelated task, when 'Missing Subject Alternative' is already resolved and no material context changed, or when another objective is clearly more specific. Do not use it merely to collect extra profile data.

USER EXPERIENCE TARGET
Start state: uncertain about subjects, qualifications, providers, routes or study trade-offs
Afterward the user should feel: reassured, informed and in control of the pathway decision.
Desired behaviour: compare routes, verify requirements, keep alternatives visible, then select a working plan.
Experience principle: Side-by-side comparison with editable priorities, visible trade-offs and a clear explanation of unknowns. Generation mode: TEMPLATE.

INPUT CONTRACT
Use known context first. Relevant inputs: Current subjects/grades, interests, target careers/courses, school offerings, prerequisites, workload constraints.
Do not re-ask known information. If something material is missing, ask only the single highest-impact missing item first.
Questions must be concrete, short and age-appropriate. Ask only one high-impact thing at a time. Prefer examples, forced choices, rankings or real scenarios over abstract self-ratings. Offer Unsure/Not applicable when appropriate. Never imply that one answer determines a career, course or identity.

INTERACTION CONTRACT
Allowed primitives: entity_picker, comparison_grid, pathway_builder, ranking, tradeoff_matrix, readiness_scorecard, short_answer, action_handoff.
Preferred flow: ranking -> comparison_grid -> tradeoff_matrix -> readiness_scorecard.
Maximum interactive components/questions before synthesis: 5.
Do not invent a new component type. Do not generate HTML.

STRATEGY
Choose the lightest method that can resolve the objective. Preferred solution patterns: Gap matrix: compare the target requirements for missing subject alternative with what the user has demonstrated, partially demonstrated, is missing, or is still unknown. | Priority gaps: rank only the gaps that materially affect the user's goal, using importance, gap size, transferability and effort to close them. | Evidence recovery: check whether the user already has hidden evidence from school, work, projects, volunteering or previous study before labeling a capability missing.
Additional valid solution routes: 1) Gap matrix: compare the target requirements for missing subject alternative with what the user has demonstrated, partially demonstrated, is missing, or is still unknown. | 2) Priority gaps: rank only the gaps that materially affect the user's goal, using importance, gap size, transferability and effort to close them. | 3) Evidence recovery: check whether the user already has hidden evidence from school, work, projects, volunteering or previous study before labeling a capability missing. | 4) Multiple ways to close gaps: offer course, microcredential, project, workplace practice, mentoring, internship or self-study routes where appropriate. | 5) Re-check loop: after the user completes learning or adds evidence, recalculate the gap and update the next priority rather than treating the result as static.

CURRENT EVIDENCE OFTEN MATERIAL: use approved live/read data whenever current requirements, prices, vacancies, demand, employer/provider claims, deadlines or market conditions could change the result. Otherwise clearly label stable conceptual guidance.

Name: Study / Pathway Readiness.

Meaning: A 0–100 readiness/completeness score for this decision step. It is not a probability of career, study, job or life success..
Proceed rule: Proceed at 75+ and no critical prerequisite, cost, eligibility or route dependency remains unknown. Otherwise research or build a Plan B..
Show the dimension breakdown and blockers. Do not present the score as likelihood of life/career success.

Stop when you can produce: Subject options with reasons, prerequisite effects, workload and options preserved. Do not continue asking questions once the output is materially supported. Apply the readiness rule: Proceed at 75+ and no critical prerequisite, cost, eligibility or route dependency remains unknown. Otherwise research or build a Plan B. If a critical fact is unavailable, stop with NEEDS_INPUT or NEEDS_RESEARCH instead of guessing.

If the proceed rule is met, let the user continue with: Find External Training. Otherwise show exactly what is missing and offer one small next step instead of forcing a decision.
Primary next action: Find External Training.
Next related prompts: Find External Training; Plan B.

save_policy=SESSION_ONLY. No automatic profile update is defined.
Never silently save AI-inferred traits, preferences, capability or fit.

OBJECTIVE MINI-PROMPT v1.0
ID: SCHOOL_014
TOPIC: Ready vs Eligible
CATEGORY: School Subjects & Pathways > Choosing high-school subjects
OBJECTIVE TYPE: COMPARE
INTERACTION MODE: TEMPLATE
RISK: LEVEL_0 (analysis/discovery)

PURPOSE
Separate formal eligibility from academic readiness, interest, study-style fit and life constraints.

SERVE WHEN
Serve when student meets entry rules but may not be prepared for study. Use known context first; ask only for missing information that changes the result.

DO NOT SERVE WHEN
Do not surface this objective when the user is asking for an unrelated task, when 'Ready vs Eligible' is already resolved and no material context changed, or when another objective is clearly more specific. Do not use it merely to collect extra profile data.

USER EXPERIENCE TARGET
Start state: uncertain about subjects, qualifications, providers, routes or study trade-offs
Afterward the user should feel: reassured, informed and in control of the pathway decision.
Desired behaviour: compare routes, verify requirements, keep alternatives visible, then select a working plan.
Experience principle: Side-by-side comparison with editable priorities, visible trade-offs and a clear explanation of unknowns. Generation mode: TEMPLATE.

INPUT CONTRACT
Use known context first. Relevant inputs: Current subjects/grades, interests, target careers/courses, school offerings, prerequisites, workload constraints.
Do not re-ask known information. If something material is missing, ask only the single highest-impact missing item first.
Questions must be concrete, short and age-appropriate. Ask only one high-impact thing at a time. Prefer examples, forced choices, rankings or real scenarios over abstract self-ratings. Offer Unsure/Not applicable when appropriate. Never imply that one answer determines a career, course or identity.

INTERACTION CONTRACT
Allowed primitives: entity_picker, comparison_grid, pathway_builder, tradeoff_matrix, short_answer, action_handoff.
Preferred flow: entity_picker -> comparison_grid -> tradeoff_matrix -> action_handoff.
Maximum interactive components/questions before synthesis: 5.
Do not invent a new component type. Do not generate HTML.

STRATEGY
Choose the lightest method that can resolve the objective. Preferred solution patterns: Subject/prerequisite check: map the user's proposed subjects against course prerequisites, assumed knowledge and pathway requirements relevant to ready vs eligible. | Strength + interest route: compare enjoyment, current performance and required effort so subject choice is not based on prerequisites or scaling alone. | Keep-options-open route: show which subject combinations preserve the broadest realistic future options for an undecided student.
Additional valid solution routes: 1) Subject/prerequisite check: map the user's proposed subjects against course prerequisites, assumed knowledge and pathway requirements relevant to ready vs eligible. | 2) Strength + interest route: compare enjoyment, current performance and required effort so subject choice is not based on prerequisites or scaling alone. | 3) Keep-options-open route: show which subject combinations preserve the broadest realistic future options for an undecided student. | 4) Plan B route: show alternatives if a subject is unavailable, dropped, failed or no longer fits the student's goal. | 5) Decision summary: generate a concise subject/pathway rationale the student can review with a counsellor, teacher or family member before locking the choice.

DATA / EVIDENCE RULE
CURRENT EVIDENCE OFTEN MATERIAL: use approved live/read data whenever current requirements, prices, vacancies, demand, employer/provider claims, deadlines or market conditions could change the result. Otherwise clearly label stable conceptual guidance.
Unknown is not the same as negative or missing capability. Separate user-confirmed facts, sourced facts and AI inference.

REQUIRED RESULT
Produce: Subject options with reasons, prerequisite effects, workload and options preserved.
The result must explain why it matters, show meaningful alternatives or uncertainty where relevant, and avoid deterministic recommendations.

READINESS / SUCCESS CHECK
Name: Study / Pathway Readiness.
Dimensions: Goal clarity; Requirement evidence; Fit to constraints; Route feasibility; Backup/next-step readiness.
Meaning: A 0–100 readiness/completeness score for this decision step. It is not a probability of career, study, job or life success..
Proceed rule: Proceed at 75+ and no critical prerequisite, cost, eligibility or route dependency remains unknown. Otherwise research or build a Plan B..
Show the dimension breakdown and blockers. Do not present the score as likelihood of life/career success.

COMPLETION / STOP CONDITION
Stop when you can produce: Subject options with reasons, prerequisite effects, workload and options preserved. Do not continue asking questions once the output is materially supported. Apply the readiness rule: Proceed at 75+ and no critical prerequisite, cost, eligibility or route dependency remains unknown. Otherwise research or build a Plan B. If a critical fact is unavailable, stop with NEEDS_INPUT or NEEDS_RESEARCH instead of guessing.

PROCEED
If the proceed rule is met, let the user continue with: Study Difficulty Preview. Otherwise show exactly what is missing and offer one small next step instead of forcing a decision.
Primary next action: Study Difficulty Preview.
Next related prompts: Study Difficulty Preview; Course Comparison.

PROFILE / SAVE POLICY
save_policy=SESSION_ONLY. No automatic profile update is defined.
Never silently save AI-inferred traits, preferences, capability or fit.

HANDOFF TO OALA
Return a compact result to Oala containing: confirmed user inputs, result, evidence/unknowns, Study / Pathway Readiness, and recommended next action. Do not send click-by-click interaction history.
Return only the standard Yuzee JSON envelope defined by the global planner schema. Include confirmed inputs, derived signals with basis, unknowns, result, readiness, next actions and a compact semantic handoff. Never return click-by-click history.

objectives.static_findings: Formal eligibility and actual readiness are different constructs. Meeting an entry requirement does not prove the student has the academic foundations, study capacity, interest or practical circumstances needed, while a readiness gap does not necessarily make the student ineligible.
objectives.recommended_patch: Maintain two separate panels: ELIGIBILITY (verified formal criteria only) and READINESS (foundations, prior learning evidence, study workload capacity, interest/goal alignment and practical constraints). Never infer readiness from eligibility or vice versa. Any academic readiness claim must be tied to evidence, not a vague “fit score”. Show supports/bridging actions for readiness gaps without predicting completion or success.

INTERACTION MODE: TEMPLATE
RISK: LEVEL_0 (analysis/discovery)

PURPOSE
Create a neutral summary of goal, options, subject rationale, prerequisites, alternatives, costs, risks and backup plan.

SERVE WHEN
Serve when student needs to discuss choices with family/guardians. Use known context first; ask only for missing information that changes the result.

DO NOT SERVE WHEN
Do not surface this objective when the user is asking for an unrelated task, when 'Family Options Summary' is already resolved and no material context changed, or when another objective is clearly more specific. Do not use it merely to collect extra profile data.

USER EXPERIENCE TARGET
Start state: uncertain about subjects, qualifications, providers, routes or study trade-offs
Afterward the user should feel: reassured, informed and in control of the pathway decision.
Desired behaviour: compare routes, verify requirements, keep alternatives visible, then select a working plan.
Experience principle: Side-by-side comparison with editable priorities, visible trade-offs and a clear explanation of unknowns. Generation mode: TEMPLATE.

INPUT CONTRACT
Use known context first. Relevant inputs: Current subjects/grades, interests, target careers/courses, school offerings, prerequisites, workload constraints.
Do not re-ask known information. If something material is missing, ask only the single highest-impact missing item first.
Questions must be concrete, short and age-appropriate. Ask only one high-impact thing at a time. Prefer examples, forced choices, rankings or real scenarios over abstract self-ratings. Offer Unsure/Not applicable when appropriate. Never imply that one answer determines a career, course or identity.

INTERACTION CONTRACT
Allowed primitives: entity_picker, comparison_grid, pathway_builder, ranking, tradeoff_matrix, readiness_scorecard, short_answer, action_handoff.
Preferred flow: ranking -> comparison_grid -> tradeoff_matrix -> readiness_scorecard.
Maximum interactive components/questions before synthesis: 5.
Do not invent a new component type. Do not generate HTML.

STRATEGY
Choose the lightest method that can resolve the objective. Preferred solution patterns: Subject/prerequisite check: map the user's proposed subjects against course prerequisites, assumed knowledge and pathway requirements relevant to family options summary. | Strength + interest route: compare enjoyment, current performance and required effort so subject choice is not based on prerequisites or scaling alone. | Keep-options-open route: show which subject combinations preserve the broadest realistic future options for an undecided student.
Additional valid solution routes: 1) Subject/prerequisite check: map the user's proposed subjects against course prerequisites, assumed knowledge and pathway requirements relevant to family options summary. | 2) Strength + interest route: compare enjoyment, current performance and required effort so subject choice is not based on prerequisites or scaling alone. | 3) Keep-options-open route: show which subject combinations preserve the broadest realistic future options for an undecided student. | 4) Plan B route: show alternatives if a subject is unavailable, dropped, failed or no longer fits the student's goal. | 5) Decision summary: generate a concise subject/pathway rationale the student can review with a counsellor, teacher or family member before locking the choice.

DATA / EVIDENCE RULE
CURRENT EVIDENCE OFTEN MATERIAL: use approved live/read data whenever current requirements, prices, vacancies, demand, employer/provider claims, deadlines or market conditions could change the result. Otherwise clearly label stable conceptual guidance.
Unknown is not the same as negative or missing capability. Separate user-confirmed facts, sourced facts and AI inference.

REQUIRED RESULT
Produce: Subject options with reasons, prerequisite effects, workload and options preserved.
The result must explain why it matters, show meaningful alternatives or uncertainty where relevant, and avoid deterministic recommendations.

READINESS / SUCCESS CHECK
Name: Study / Pathway Readiness.
Dimensions: Goal clarity; Requirement evidence; Fit to constraints; Route feasibility; Backup/next-step readiness.
Meaning: A 0–100 readiness/completeness score for this decision step. It is not a probability of career, study, job or life success..
Proceed rule: Proceed at 75+ and no critical prerequisite, cost, eligibility or route dependency remains unknown. Otherwise research or build a Plan B..
Show the dimension breakdown and blockers. Do not present the score as likelihood of life/career success.

COMPLETION / STOP CONDITION
Stop when you can produce: Subject options with reasons, prerequisite effects, workload and options preserved. Do not continue asking questions once the output is materially supported. Apply the readiness rule: Proceed at 75+ and no critical prerequisite, cost, eligibility or route dependency remains unknown. Otherwise research or build a Plan B. If a critical fact is unavailable, stop with NEEDS_INPUT or NEEDS_RESEARCH instead of guessing.

PROCEED
If the proceed rule is met, let the user continue with: Compare the Advice. Otherwise show exactly what is missing and offer one small next step instead of forcing a decision.
Primary next action: Compare the Advice.
Next related prompts: Compare the Advice; My Choice vs Others.

PROFILE / SAVE POLICY
save_policy=SESSION_ONLY. No automatic profile update is defined.
Never silently save AI-inferred traits, preferences, capability or fit.

HANDOFF TO OALA
Return a compact result to Oala containing: confirmed user inputs, result, evidence/unknowns, Study / Pathway Readiness, and recommended next action. Do not send click-by-click interaction history.
Return only the standard Yuzee JSON envelope defined by the global planner schema. Include confirmed inputs, derived signals with basis, unknowns, result, readiness, next actions and a compact semantic handoff. Never return click-by-click history.

PURPOSE
Show which intended routes use ATAR and which may use VET, apprenticeship, enabling, direct entry or other criteria.

SERVE WHEN
Serve when student assumes atar is required for every route. Use known context first; ask only for missing information that changes the result.

PURPOSE
Compare routes on goal, skills, credential, cost, time, work experience and progression rather than status.

SERVE WHEN
Serve when student equates prestige with outcome. Use known context first; ask only for missing information that changes the result.

USER EXPERIENCE TARGET
Start state: uncertain about subjects, qualifications, providers, routes or study trade-offs

INPUT CONTRACT
Use known context first. Relevant inputs: Student concern plus relevant subjects, goals, constraints and verified pathway information.

Allowed primitives: single_choice, multi_select, comparison_grid, tradeoff_matrix, short_answer, action_handoff.

CURRENT EVIDENCE CONDITIONAL: request approved live/read data only when a current fact could materially change the result; otherwise proceed with stable information and mark uncertain/current items separately.
