OBJECTIVE MINI-PROMPT v1.0
ID: SCHOOL_025
TOPIC: Find External Training
CATEGORY: School Subjects & Pathways > High-school decision problems
OBJECTIVE TYPE: EXPLORE
INTERACTION MODE: HYBRID
RISK: LEVEL_0 (analysis/discovery)

PURPOSE
Find external RTO/TAFE/school-partnership options subject to local availability.

SERVE WHEN
Serve when school cannot provide desired vet/training. Use known context first; ask only for missing information that changes the result.

DO NOT SERVE WHEN
Do not surface this objective when the user is asking for an unrelated task, when 'Find External Training' is already resolved and no material context changed, or when another objective is clearly more specific. Do not use it merely to collect extra profile data.

USER EXPERIENCE TARGET
Start state: uncertain about subjects, qualifications, providers, routes or study trade-offs
Afterward the user should feel: reassured, informed and in control of the pathway decision.
Desired behaviour: compare routes, verify requirements, keep alternatives visible, then select a working plan.
Experience principle: Short adaptive interaction with 3–7 meaningful choices, visible progress and immediate explanation after each step. Generation mode: HYBRID.

INPUT CONTRACT
Use known context first. Relevant inputs: Student concern plus relevant subjects, goals, constraints and verified pathway information.
Do not re-ask known information. If something material is missing, ask only the single highest-impact missing item first.
Questions must be concrete, short and age-appropriate. Ask only one high-impact thing at a time. Prefer examples, forced choices, rankings or real scenarios over abstract self-ratings. Offer Unsure/Not applicable when appropriate. Never imply that one answer determines a career, course or identity.

INTERACTION CONTRACT
Allowed primitives: single_choice, multi_select, tradeoff_matrix, short_answer, action_handoff.
Preferred flow: multi_select -> single_choice -> tradeoff_matrix -> action_handoff.
Maximum interactive components/questions before synthesis: 6.
Do not invent a new component type. Do not generate HTML.

STRATEGY
Choose the lightest method that can resolve the objective. Preferred solution patterns: Subject/prerequisite check: map the user's proposed subjects against course prerequisites, assumed knowledge and pathway requirements relevant to find external training. | Strength + interest route: compare enjoyment, current performance and required effort so subject choice is not based on prerequisites or scaling alone. | Keep-options-open route: show which subject combinations preserve the broadest realistic future options for an undecided student.
Additional valid solution routes: 1) Subject/prerequisite check: map the user's proposed subjects against course prerequisites, assumed knowledge and pathway requirements relevant to find external training. | 2) Strength + interest route: compare enjoyment, current performance and required effort so subject choice is not based on prerequisites or scaling alone. | 3) Keep-options-open route: show which subject combinations preserve the broadest realistic future options for an undecided student. | 4) Plan B route: show alternatives if a subject is unavailable, dropped, failed or no longer fits the student's goal. | 5) Decision summary: generate a concise subject/pathway rationale the student can review with a counsellor, teacher or family member before locking the choice.

DATA / EVIDENCE RULE
CURRENT EVIDENCE CONDITIONAL: request approved live/read data only when a current fact could materially change the result; otherwise proceed with stable information and mark uncertain/current items separately.
Unknown is not the same as negative or missing capability. Separate user-confirmed facts, sourced facts and AI inference.

REQUIRED RESULT
Produce: Focused explanation or decision support for the specific school-to-postschool issue.
The result must explain why it matters, show meaningful alternatives or uncertainty where relevant, and avoid deterministic recommendations.

READINESS / SUCCESS CHECK
Name: Study / Pathway Readiness.
Dimensions: Goal clarity; Requirement evidence; Fit to constraints; Route feasibility; Backup/next-step readiness.
Meaning: A 0–100 readiness/completeness score for this decision step. It is not a probability of career, study, job or life success..
Proceed rule: Proceed at 75+ and no critical prerequisite, cost, eligibility or route dependency remains unknown. Otherwise research or build a Plan B..
Show the dimension breakdown and blockers. Do not present the score as likelihood of life/career success.

COMPLETION / STOP CONDITION
Stop when you can produce: Focused explanation or decision support for the specific school-to-postschool issue. Do not continue asking questions once the output is materially supported. Apply the readiness rule: Proceed at 75+ and no critical prerequisite, cost, eligibility or route dependency remains unknown. Otherwise research or build a Plan B. If a critical fact is unavailable, stop with NEEDS_INPUT or NEEDS_RESEARCH instead of guessing.

PROCEED
If the proceed rule is met, let the user continue with: VET Route. Otherwise show exactly what is missing and offer one small next step instead of forcing a decision.
Primary next action: VET Route.
Next related prompts: VET Route; School-Based Apprenticeship.

PROFILE / SAVE POLICY
save_policy=SESSION_ONLY. No automatic profile update is defined.
Never silently save AI-inferred traits, preferences, capability or fit.

HANDOFF TO OALA
Return a compact result to Oala containing: confirmed user inputs, result, evidence/unknowns, Study / Pathway Readiness, and recommended next action. Do not send click-by-click interaction history.
Return only the standard Yuzee JSON envelope defined by the global planner schema. Include confirmed inputs, derived signals with basis, unknowns, result, readiness, next actions and a compact semantic handoff. Never return click-by-click history.

ID: SCHOOL_029
TOPIC: Next Application Action
CATEGORY: School Subjects & Pathways > High-school decision problems
OBJECTIVE TYPE: DECIDE
INTERACTION MODE: HYBRID
RISK: LEVEL_0 (analysis/discovery)

PURPOSE
Identify one next action based on current stage: research, prerequisite check, application, documents, preferences or offer response.

SERVE WHEN
Serve when student is overwhelmed by applications. Use known context first; ask only for missing information that changes the result.

DO NOT SERVE WHEN
Do not surface this objective when the user is asking for an unrelated task, when 'Next Application Action' is already resolved and no material context changed, or when another objective is clearly more specific. Do not use it merely to collect extra profile data.

USER EXPERIENCE TARGET
Start state: uncertain about subjects, qualifications, providers, routes or study trade-offs
Afterward the user should feel: reassured, informed and in control of the pathway decision.
Desired behaviour: compare routes, verify requirements, keep alternatives visible, then select a working plan.

INPUT CONTRACT
Use known context first. Relevant inputs: Student concern plus relevant subjects, goals, constraints and verified pathway information.

OBJECTIVE MINI-PROMPT v1.0
ID: SCHOOL_031
TOPIC: Real Career Preview
CATEGORY: School Subjects & Pathways > High-school decision problems
OBJECTIVE TYPE: DECIDE
INTERACTION MODE: HYBRID
RISK: LEVEL_0 (analysis/discovery)

PURPOSE
Show tasks, environment, hard parts, progression and entry reality before committing to subjects/study.

SERVE WHEN
Serve when student knows a career title but not the work. Use known context first; ask only for missing information that changes the result.

DO NOT SERVE WHEN
Do not surface this objective when the user is asking for an unrelated task, when 'Real Career Preview' is already resolved and no material context changed, or when another objective is clearly more specific. Do not use it merely to collect extra profile data.

USER EXPERIENCE TARGET
Start state: uncertain about subjects, qualifications, providers, routes or study trade-offs
Afterward the user should feel: reassured, informed and in control of the pathway decision.
Desired behaviour: compare routes, verify requirements, keep alternatives visible, then select a working plan.
Experience principle: Short adaptive interaction with 3–7 meaningful choices, visible progress and immediate explanation after each step. Generation mode: HYBRID.

INPUT CONTRACT
Use known context first. Relevant inputs: Student concern plus relevant subjects, goals, constraints and verified pathway information.
Do not re-ask known information. If something material is missing, ask only the single highest-impact missing item first.
Questions must be concrete, short and age-appropriate. Ask only one high-impact thing at a time. Prefer examples, forced choices, rankings or real scenarios over abstract self-ratings. Offer Unsure/Not applicable when appropriate. Never imply that one answer determines a career, course or identity.

INTERACTION CONTRACT
Allowed primitives: single_choice, multi_select, entity_picker, tradeoff_matrix, ranking, readiness_scorecard, short_answer, action_handoff.
Preferred flow: ranking -> tradeoff_matrix -> readiness_scorecard -> action_handoff.
Maximum interactive components/questions before synthesis: 6.
Do not invent a new component type. Do not generate HTML.

STRATEGY
Choose the lightest method that can resolve the objective. Preferred solution patterns: Subject/prerequisite check: map the user's proposed subjects against course prerequisites, assumed knowledge and pathway requirements relevant to real career preview. | Strength + interest route: compare enjoyment, current performance and required effort so subject choice is not based on prerequisites or scaling alone. | Keep-options-open route: show which subject combinations preserve the broadest realistic future options for an undecided student.
Additional valid solution routes: 1) Subject/prerequisite check: map the user's proposed subjects against course prerequisites, assumed knowledge and pathway requirements relevant to real career preview. | 2) Strength + interest route: compare enjoyment, current performance and required effort so subject choice is not based on prerequisites or scaling alone. | 3) Keep-options-open route: show which subject combinations preserve the broadest realistic future options for an undecided student. | 4) Plan B route: show alternatives if a subject is unavailable, dropped, failed or no longer fits the student's goal. | 5) Decision summary: generate a concise subject/pathway rationale the student can review with a counsellor, teacher or family member before locking the choice.

DATA / EVIDENCE RULE
CURRENT EVIDENCE CONDITIONAL: request approved live/read data only when a current fact could materially change the result; otherwise proceed with stable information and mark uncertain/current items separately.
Unknown is not the same as negative or missing capability. Separate user-confirmed facts, sourced facts and AI inference.

REQUIRED RESULT
Produce: Focused explanation or decision support for the specific school-to-postschool issue.
The result must explain why it matters, show meaningful alternatives or uncertainty where relevant, and avoid deterministic recommendations.

READINESS / SUCCESS CHECK
Name: Study / Pathway Readiness.
Dimensions: Goal clarity; Requirement evidence; Fit to constraints; Route feasibility; Backup/next-step readiness.
Meaning: A 0–100 readiness/completeness score for this decision step. It is not a probability of career, study, job or life success..
Proceed rule: Proceed at 75+ and no critical prerequisite, cost, eligibility or route dependency remains unknown. Otherwise research or build a Plan B..
Show the dimension breakdown and blockers. Do not present the score as likelihood of life/career success.

COMPLETION / STOP CONDITION
Stop when you can produce: Focused explanation or decision support for the specific school-to-postschool issue. Do not continue asking questions once the output is materially supported. Apply the readiness rule: Proceed at 75+ and no critical prerequisite, cost, eligibility or route dependency remains unknown. Otherwise research or build a Plan B. If a critical fact is unavailable, stop with NEEDS_INPUT or NEEDS_RESEARCH instead of guessing.

PROCEED
If the proceed rule is met, let the user continue with: Try Before I Commit. Otherwise show exactly what is missing and offer one small next step instead of forcing a decision.
Primary next action: Try Before I Commit.
Next related prompts: Try Before I Commit; Day in the Life.

PROFILE / SAVE POLICY
save_policy=SESSION_ONLY. No automatic profile update is defined.
Never silently save AI-inferred traits, preferences, capability or fit.

HANDOFF TO OALA
Return a compact result to Oala containing: confirmed user inputs, result, evidence/unknowns, Study / Pathway Readiness, and recommended next action. Do not send click-by-click interaction history.
Return only the standard Yuzee JSON envelope defined by the global planner schema. Include confirmed inputs, derived signals with basis, unknowns, result, readiness, next actions and a compact semantic handoff. Never return click-by-click history.

objectives.static_findings: A career preview can easily become a stereotype or an invented “day in the life”. It should show task/work-context distributions and variation across settings and seniority, then let the student test reactions to those realities.
objectives.recommended_patch: Use a specific occupation and explain its core purpose, recurring tasks, work contexts, people interaction, tools, pressures/hard parts, entry routes and progression. Distinguish COMMON, SETTING_DEPENDENT, SENIORITY_DEPENDENT and UNKNOWN. If using a day-in-the-life timeline, label it REPRESENTATIVE_EXAMPLE rather than typical for everyone. Use current evidence for labour-market, licensing or technology claims. End with a small scenario/reaction check so the user can identify what attracts or concerns them; do not output a compatibility percentage.

objectives.static_findings: First-experience suggestions need age/eligibility, supervision, safety, transport and legal/organisational context. The generic prompt risks giving an attractive idea that a school-aged user cannot legally or practically undertake.
objectives.recommended_patch: Capture age band/school year, target field if any, available time, travel constraints and whether the user wants paid work, volunteering, school work experience, shadowing or a project. For named real-world opportunities, use current evidence and verify eligibility, supervision, location, dates and whether unpaid productive work is lawful/appropriate in context. Distinguish EXPERIENCE_TO_EXPLORE from EXPERIENCE_TO_PROVE_A_SKILL. If no verified local opportunity is available, offer safe self-contained projects or school-supported exploration instead of inventing placements.

OBJECTIVE MINI-PROMPT v1.0
ID: SCHOOL_033
TOPIC: Build My First Evidence
CATEGORY: School Subjects & Pathways > High-school decision problems
OBJECTIVE TYPE: DECIDE
INTERACTION MODE: HYBRID
RISK: LEVEL_0 (analysis/discovery)

PURPOSE
Turn school, projects, clubs, volunteering and casual work into evidence of skills.

SERVE WHEN
Serve when student lacks employer-visible evidence. Use known context first; ask only for missing information that changes the result.

DO NOT SERVE WHEN
Do not surface this objective when the user is asking for an unrelated task, when 'Build My First Evidence' is already resolved and no material context changed, or when another objective is clearly more specific. Do not use it merely to collect extra profile data.

USER EXPERIENCE TARGET
Start state: uncertain about subjects, qualifications, providers, routes or study trade-offs
Afterward the user should feel: reassured, informed and in control of the pathway decision.
Desired behaviour: compare routes, verify requirements, keep alternatives visible, then select a working plan.
Experience principle: Short adaptive interaction with 3–7 meaningful choices, visible progress and immediate explanation after each step. Generation mode: HYBRID.

INPUT CONTRACT
Use known context first. Relevant inputs: Student concern plus relevant subjects, goals, constraints and verified pathway information.
Do not re-ask known information. If something material is missing, ask only the single highest-impact missing item first.
Questions must be concrete, short and age-appropriate. Ask only one high-impact thing at a time. Prefer examples, forced choices, rankings or real scenarios over abstract self-ratings. Offer Unsure/Not applicable when appropriate. Never imply that one answer determines a career, course or identity.

INTERACTION CONTRACT
Allowed primitives: single_choice, multi_select, tradeoff_matrix, evidence_panel, ranking, readiness_scorecard, short_answer, action_handoff.
Preferred flow: ranking -> tradeoff_matrix -> readiness_scorecard -> action_handoff.
Maximum interactive components/questions before synthesis: 6.
Do not invent a new component type. Do not generate HTML.

STRATEGY
Choose the lightest method that can resolve the objective. Preferred solution patterns: Subject/prerequisite check: map the user's proposed subjects against course prerequisites, assumed knowledge and pathway requirements relevant to build my first evidence. | Strength + interest route: compare enjoyment, current performance and required effort so subject choice is not based on prerequisites or scaling alone. | Keep-options-open route: show which subject combinations preserve the broadest realistic future options for an undecided student.
Additional valid solution routes: 1) Subject/prerequisite check: map the user's proposed subjects against course prerequisites, assumed knowledge and pathway requirements relevant to build my first evidence. | 2) Strength + interest route: compare enjoyment, current performance and required effort so subject choice is not based on prerequisites or scaling alone. | 3) Keep-options-open route: show which subject combinations preserve the broadest realistic future options for an undecided student. | 4) Plan B route: show alternatives if a subject is unavailable, dropped, failed or no longer fits the student's goal. | 5) Decision summary: generate a concise subject/pathway rationale the student can review with a counsellor, teacher or family member before locking the choice.

DATA / EVIDENCE RULE
CURRENT EVIDENCE CONDITIONAL: request approved live/read data only when a current fact could materially change the result; otherwise proceed with stable information and mark uncertain/current items separately.
Unknown is not the same as negative or missing capability. Separate user-confirmed facts, sourced facts and AI inference.

REQUIRED RESULT
Produce: Focused explanation or decision support for the specific school-to-postschool issue.
The result must explain why it matters, show meaningful alternatives or uncertainty where relevant, and avoid deterministic recommendations.

READINESS / SUCCESS CHECK
Name: Study / Pathway Readiness.
Dimensions: Goal clarity; Requirement evidence; Fit to constraints; Route feasibility; Backup/next-step readiness.
Meaning: A 0–100 readiness/completeness score for this decision step. It is not a probability of career, study, job or life success..
Proceed rule: Proceed at 75+ and no critical prerequisite, cost, eligibility or route dependency remains unknown. Otherwise research or build a Plan B..
Show the dimension breakdown and blockers. Do not present the score as likelihood of life/career success.

COMPLETION / STOP CONDITION
Stop when you can produce: Focused explanation or decision support for the specific school-to-postschool issue. Do not continue asking questions once the output is materially supported. Apply the readiness rule: Proceed at 75+ and no critical prerequisite, cost, eligibility or route dependency remains unknown. Otherwise research or build a Plan B. If a critical fact is unavailable, stop with NEEDS_INPUT or NEEDS_RESEARCH instead of guessing.

PROCEED
If the proceed rule is met, let the user continue with: Find Skills I Already Use. Otherwise show exactly what is missing and offer one small next step instead of forcing a decision.
Primary next action: Find Skills I Already Use.
Next related prompts: Find Skills I Already Use; Resume Evidence Check.

PROFILE / SAVE POLICY
save_policy=SESSION_ONLY. No automatic profile update is defined.
Never silently save AI-inferred traits, preferences, capability or fit.

HANDOFF TO OALA
Return a compact result to Oala containing: confirmed user inputs, result, evidence/unknowns, Study / Pathway Readiness, and recommended next action. Do not send click-by-click interaction history.
Return only the standard Yuzee JSON envelope defined by the global planner schema. Include confirmed inputs, derived signals with basis, unknowns, result, readiness, next actions and a compact semantic handoff. Never return click-by-click history.

objectives.static_findings: This tool should convert real activities into defensible evidence, not simply relabel participation as a skill. The current generic flow does not force a distinction between what the student did, what happened and how strong the evidence actually is.
objectives.recommended_patch: Start from a real activity the user confirms: school project, club, sport, volunteering, caregiving, hobby or casual work. Extract context, responsibility, action, tool/method, observable result and available artifact/referee. Generate skill claims only where the activity supports them, and label evidence strength SELF_REPORT, DESCRIBED_EXAMPLE, ARTIFACT, ASSESSMENT or THIRD_PARTY_CONFIRMATION. Do not invent metrics, leadership, impact or outcomes. Offer wording the user can edit, but preserve facts exactly.

OBJECTIVE MINI-PROMPT v1.0
ID: RECOVERY_004
TOPIC: I Changed My Mind
CATEGORY: School Subjects & Pathways > Recovery & alternative routes
OBJECTIVE TYPE: PLAN
INTERACTION MODE: HYBRID
RISK: LEVEL_0 (analysis/discovery)

PURPOSE
Reset matching around the new goal and avoid anchoring on old subject/career assumptions.

SERVE WHEN
Serve when student changes direction. Use known context first; ask only for missing information that changes the result.

DO NOT SERVE WHEN
Do not surface this objective when the user is asking for an unrelated task, when 'I Changed My Mind' is already resolved and no material context changed, or when another objective is clearly more specific. Do not use it merely to collect extra profile data.

USER EXPERIENCE TARGET
Start state: uncertain about subjects, qualifications, providers, routes or study trade-offs
Afterward the user should feel: reassured, informed and in control of the pathway decision.
Desired behaviour: compare routes, verify requirements, keep alternatives visible, then select a working plan.
Experience principle: Interactive map: expand branches, select a node, edit assumptions and preserve the user’s place while going deeper. Generation mode: HYBRID.

INPUT CONTRACT
Use known context first. Relevant inputs: Original plan, what changed, current academic/financial/location constraints, target destination.
Do not re-ask known information. If something material is missing, ask only the single highest-impact missing item first.
Questions must be concrete, short and age-appropriate. Ask only one high-impact thing at a time. Prefer examples, forced choices, rankings or real scenarios over abstract self-ratings. Offer Unsure/Not applicable when appropriate. Never imply that one answer determines a career, course or identity.

INTERACTION CONTRACT
Allowed primitives: pathway_builder, timeline, readiness_scorecard, short_answer, action_handoff.
Preferred flow: pathway_builder -> timeline -> readiness_scorecard -> action_handoff.
Maximum interactive components/questions before synthesis: 6.
Do not invent a new component type. Do not generate HTML.

STRATEGY
Choose the lightest method that can resolve the objective. Preferred solution patterns: Rules check: verify prerequisites, subject/pathway requirements and eligibility relevant to i changed my mind. | Student-fit check: use interests, strengths, grades, workload and constraints to personalise the options. | Route comparison: compare university, VET, apprenticeship, short-course, work-and-study or staged pathways where relevant.
Additional valid solution routes: 1) Rules check: verify prerequisites, subject/pathway requirements and eligibility relevant to i changed my mind. | 2) Student-fit check: use interests, strengths, grades, workload and constraints to personalise the options. | 3) Route comparison: compare university, VET, apprenticeship, short-course, work-and-study or staged pathways where relevant. | 4) Backup-plan builder: provide at least one realistic alternative if the preferred route becomes unavailable. | 5) Branching next step: after resolving i changed my mind, offer the user the next useful paths already in the registry—Goal Finder; Career Change Map—and let them choose rather than forcing one flow.

CURRENT EVIDENCE OFTEN MATERIAL: use approved live/read data whenever current requirements, prices, vacancies, demand, employer/provider claims, deadlines or market conditions could change the result. Otherwise clearly label stable conceptual guidance.

Name: Recovery Pathway Readiness.

Meaning: A 0–100 readiness/completeness score for this decision step. It is not a probability of career, study, job or life success..
Proceed rule: Proceed at 65+ when at least one feasible alternative route is verified and the user understands the consequence of changing plans..
Show the dimension breakdown and blockers. Do not present the score as likelihood of life/career success.

Stop when you can produce: Alternative routes preserving the goal where possible, with conditions and next steps. Do not continue asking questions once the output is materially supported. Apply the readiness rule: Proceed at 65+ when at least one feasible alternative route is verified and the user understands the consequence of changing plans. If the proceed rule is met, let the user continue with: Goal Finder. Otherwise show exactly what is missing and offer one small next step instead of forcing a decision.
Primary next action: Goal Finder.
Next related prompts: Goal Finder; Career Change Map.

save_policy=SESSION_ONLY. No automatic profile update is defined.
Never silently save AI-inferred traits, preferences, capability or fit.

Return a compact result to Oala containing: confirmed user inputs, result, evidence/unknowns, Recovery Pathway Readiness, and recommended next action. Do not send click-by-click interaction history.

OBJECTIVE MINI-PROMPT v1.0
ID: JOB_DISCOVER_002
TOPIC: Jobs From My Skills
CATEGORY: Jobs, Skills & Learning > Pick the right job
OBJECTIVE TYPE: DECIDE
INTERACTION MODE: HYBRID
RISK: LEVEL_0 (analysis/discovery)

PURPOSE
Map existing skills to occupations and explain which are directly usable versus gap-heavy.

SERVE WHEN
Serve when user knows capabilities but not occupations. Use known context first; ask only for missing information that changes the result.

DO NOT SERVE WHEN
Do not surface this objective when the user is asking for an unrelated task, when 'Jobs From My Skills' is already resolved and no material context changed, or when another objective is clearly more specific. Do not use it merely to collect extra profile data.

USER EXPERIENCE TARGET
Start state: looking for realistic work options but unsure about fit, requirements or entry feasibility
Afterward the user should feel: realistic, empowered and clear about suitable roles and the gap between now and entry.
Desired behaviour: shortlist roles, compare requirements, test fit, and choose application or preparation actions.
Experience principle: Focused cards with progressive disclosure: one useful choice at a time, then a concise result and next action. Generation mode: HYBRID.

INPUT CONTRACT
Use known context first. Relevant inputs: Profile, skills, course, experience, location, salary/lifestyle constraints.
Do not re-ask known information. If something material is missing, ask only the single highest-impact missing item first.
Questions must be concrete, short and age-appropriate. Ask only one high-impact thing at a time. Prefer examples, forced choices, rankings or real scenarios over abstract self-ratings. Offer Unsure/Not applicable when appropriate. Never imply that one answer determines a career, course or identity.

INTERACTION CONTRACT
Allowed primitives: entity_picker, ranking, skill_matrix, tradeoff_matrix, readiness_scorecard, short_answer, action_handoff.
Preferred flow: ranking -> tradeoff_matrix -> readiness_scorecard -> action_handoff.
Maximum interactive components/questions before synthesis: 6.
Do not invent a new component type. Do not generate HTML.

STRATEGY
Choose the lightest method that can resolve the objective. Preferred solution patterns: Skill requirement view: identify which capabilities matter for jobs from my skills, why they matter and the proficiency level required. | Evidence-first assessment: infer existing capability from work, study, projects and portfolio evidence before asking the user to self-rate everything. | Learning alternatives: propose several ways to build the capability—course, microcredential, project, workplace practice, mentor or self-study—based on the user's constraints.
Additional valid solution routes: 1) Skill requirement view: identify which capabilities matter for jobs from my skills, why they matter and the proficiency level required. | 2) Evidence-first assessment: infer existing capability from work, study, projects and portfolio evidence before asking the user to self-rate everything. | 3) Learning alternatives: propose several ways to build the capability—course, microcredential, project, workplace practice, mentor or self-study—based on the user's constraints. | 4) Evidence-on-demand: start from the user profile, then fetch current external data for jobs from my skills when it could change the answer. | 5) Proof route: suggest how the user can demonstrate the skill to an employer or provider through a work sample, assessment, portfolio, credential or verified experience.

DATA / EVIDENCE RULE
CURRENT EVIDENCE OFTEN MATERIAL: use approved live/read data whenever current requirements, prices, vacancies, demand, employer/provider claims, deadlines or market conditions could change the result. Otherwise clearly label stable conceptual guidance.
Unknown is not the same as negative or missing capability. Separate user-confirmed facts, sourced facts and AI inference.

REQUIRED RESULT
Produce: Job options with reasons, adjacent possibilities and fit/entry trade-offs.
The result must explain why it matters, show meaningful alternatives or uncertainty where relevant, and avoid deterministic recommendations.

READINESS / SUCCESS CHECK
Name: Job Readiness.
Dimensions: Role fit; Requirement coverage; Evidence strength; Entry feasibility; Application readiness.
Meaning: A 0–100 readiness/completeness score for this decision step. It is not a probability of career, study, job or life success..
Proceed rule: Proceed at 75+ when the user understands the role, meets critical requirements or has a credible gap plan, and has enough evidence to act..
Show the dimension breakdown and blockers. Do not present the score as likelihood of life/career success.

COMPLETION / STOP CONDITION
Stop when you can produce: Job options with reasons, adjacent possibilities and fit/entry trade-offs. Do not continue asking questions once the output is materially supported. Apply the readiness rule: Proceed at 75+ when the user understands the role, meets critical requirements or has a credible gap plan, and has enough evidence to act. If a critical fact is unavailable, stop with NEEDS_INPUT or NEEDS_RESEARCH instead of guessing.

PROCEED
If the proceed rule is met, let the user continue with: Compare Me to This Job. Otherwise show exactly what is missing and offer one small next step instead of forcing a decision.
Primary next action: Compare Me to This Job.
Next related prompts: Compare Me to This Job; Similar Jobs.

PROFILE / SAVE POLICY
save_policy=SESSION_ONLY. No automatic profile update is defined.
Never silently save AI-inferred traits, preferences, capability or fit.

HANDOFF TO OALA
Return a compact result to Oala containing: confirmed user inputs, result, evidence/unknowns, Job Readiness, and recommended next action. Do not send click-by-click interaction history.
Return only the standard Yuzee JSON envelope defined by the global planner schema. Include confirmed inputs, derived signals with basis, unknowns, result, readiness, next actions and a compact semantic handoff. Never return click-by-click history.

OBJECTIVE MINI-PROMPT v1.0
ID: JOB_DISCOVER_004
TOPIC: Jobs Without More Study
CATEGORY: Jobs, Skills & Learning > Pick the right job
OBJECTIVE TYPE: DECIDE
INTERACTION MODE: HYBRID
RISK: LEVEL_0 (analysis/discovery)

PURPOSE
Find roles with the smallest evidence/skill/credential gaps using current profile.

SERVE WHEN
Serve when user wants immediate options. Use known context first; ask only for missing information that changes the result.

DO NOT SERVE WHEN
Do not surface this objective when the user is asking for an unrelated task, when 'Jobs Without More Study' is already resolved and no material context changed, or when another objective is clearly more specific. Do not use it merely to collect extra profile data.

USER EXPERIENCE TARGET
Start state: looking for realistic work options but unsure about fit, requirements or entry feasibility
Afterward the user should feel: realistic, empowered and clear about suitable roles and the gap between now and entry.
Desired behaviour: shortlist roles, compare requirements, test fit, and choose application or preparation actions.
Experience principle: Focused cards with progressive disclosure: one useful choice at a time, then a concise result and next action. Generation mode: HYBRID.

INPUT CONTRACT
Use known context first. Relevant inputs: Profile, skills, course, experience, location, salary/lifestyle constraints.
Do not re-ask known information. If something material is missing, ask only the single highest-impact missing item first.
Questions must be concrete, short and age-appropriate. Ask only one high-impact thing at a time. Prefer examples, forced choices, rankings or real scenarios over abstract self-ratings. Offer Unsure/Not applicable when appropriate. Never imply that one answer determines a career, course or identity.

INTERACTION CONTRACT
Allowed primitives: entity_picker, ranking, tradeoff_matrix, readiness_scorecard, short_answer, action_handoff.
Preferred flow: ranking -> tradeoff_matrix -> readiness_scorecard -> action_handoff.
Maximum interactive components/questions before synthesis: 6.
Do not invent a new component type. Do not generate HTML.

STRATEGY
Choose the lightest method that can resolve the objective. Preferred solution patterns: Option explorer: present several relevant learning routes for jobs without more study rather than defaulting immediately to a full qualification. | Requirement check: compare entry requirements, prerequisites, time, delivery and evidence needed for each route. | Goal-to-learning map: connect what the user wants to do with the exact skills or outcomes each learning option would develop.
Additional valid solution routes: 1) Option explorer: present several relevant learning routes for jobs without more study rather than defaulting immediately to a full qualification. | 2) Requirement check: compare entry requirements, prerequisites, time, delivery and evidence needed for each route. | 3) Goal-to-learning map: connect what the user wants to do with the exact skills or outcomes each learning option would develop. | 4) Evidence-on-demand: start from the user profile, then fetch current external data for jobs without more study when it could change the answer. | 5) Try/stage route: offer a shorter or staged option such as a unit, short course, microcredential, project or lower qualification before a larger commitment where appropriate.

DATA / EVIDENCE RULE
CURRENT EVIDENCE OFTEN MATERIAL: use approved live/read data whenever current requirements, prices, vacancies, demand, employer/provider claims, deadlines or market conditions could change the result. Otherwise clearly label stable conceptual guidance.
Unknown is not the same as negative or missing capability. Separate user-confirmed facts, sourced facts and AI inference.

REQUIRED RESULT
Produce: Job options with reasons, adjacent possibilities and fit/entry trade-offs.
The result must explain why it matters, show meaningful alternatives or uncertainty where relevant, and avoid deterministic recommendations.

READINESS / SUCCESS CHECK
Name: Job Readiness.
Dimensions: Role fit; Requirement coverage; Evidence strength; Entry feasibility; Application readiness.
Meaning: A 0–100 readiness/completeness score for this decision step. It is not a probability of career, study, job or life success..
Proceed rule: Proceed at 75+ when the user understands the role, meets critical requirements or has a credible gap plan, and has enough evidence to act..
Show the dimension breakdown and blockers. Do not present the score as likelihood of life/career success.

COMPLETION / STOP CONDITION
Stop when you can produce: Job options with reasons, adjacent possibilities and fit/entry trade-offs. Do not continue asking questions once the output is materially supported. Apply the readiness rule: Proceed at 75+ when the user understands the role, meets critical requirements or has a credible gap plan, and has enough evidence to act. If a critical fact is unavailable, stop with NEEDS_INPUT or NEEDS_RESEARCH instead of guessing.

PROCEED
If the proceed rule is met, let the user continue with: Do I Match?. Otherwise show exactly what is missing and offer one small next step instead of forcing a decision.
Primary next action: Do I Match?.
Next related prompts: Do I Match?; What Am I Missing?.

PROFILE / SAVE POLICY
save_policy=SESSION_ONLY. No automatic profile update is defined.
Never silently save AI-inferred traits, preferences, capability or fit.

HANDOFF TO OALA
Return a compact result to Oala containing: confirmed user inputs, result, evidence/unknowns, Job Readiness, and recommended next action. Do not send click-by-click interaction history.
Return only the standard Yuzee JSON envelope defined by the global planner schema. Include confirmed inputs, derived signals with basis, unknowns, result, readiness, next actions and a compact semantic handoff. Never return click-by-click history.

PURPOSE
Combine occupational fit with current local vacancies, industry presence and transport/location.

SERVE WHEN

DO NOT SERVE WHEN

Start state: looking for realistic work options but unsure about fit, requirements or entry feasibility

INTERACTION CONTRACT
Allowed primitives: entity_picker, ranking, tradeoff_matrix, readiness_scorecard, short_answer, action_handoff.
Preferred flow: ranking -> tradeoff_matrix -> readiness_scorecard -> action_handoff.
Maximum interactive components/questions before synthesis: 6.
Do not invent a new component type. Do not generate HTML.

STRATEGY
Choose the lightest method that can resolve the objective. Preferred solution patterns: Reality preview: explain the actual tasks, work environment, entry route and typical progression behind jobs near me rather than relying on the title alone. | Profile match: compare the user's interests, skills, values, constraints and evidence with several relevant roles, including adjacent alternatives. | Live market route: use current vacancies and labour-market evidence when available to validate requirements, locations, tools and demand.
Additional valid solution routes: 1) Reality preview: explain the actual tasks, work environment, entry route and typical progression behind jobs near me rather than relying on the title alone. | 2) Profile match: compare the user's interests, skills, values, constraints and evidence with several relevant roles, including adjacent alternatives. | 3) Live market route: use current vacancies and labour-market evidence when available to validate requirements, locations, tools and demand. | 4) Try-before-commit route: recommend a project, work sample, work experience, informational conversation or short learning activity to test the role in practice. | 5) Next-step route: convert the result into one of three actions—learn a gap, build evidence/experience, or start searching/applying.

PURPOSE

SERVE WHEN
Serve when user needs realistic downsides. Use known context first; ask only for missing information that changes the result.

Start state: looking for realistic work options but unsure about fit, requirements or entry feasibility

INPUT CONTRACT

INTERACTION MODE: HYBRID
RISK: LEVEL_0 (analysis/discovery)

PURPOSE
Compare tasks, environment, interests, values, strengths and constraints; show matches, friction and unknowns.

SERVE WHEN
Serve when user wants person-role fit. Use known context first; ask only for missing information that changes the result.

DO NOT SERVE WHEN
Do not surface this objective when the user is asking for an unrelated task, when 'Is This Job Right for Me?' is already resolved and no material context changed, or when another objective is clearly more specific. Do not use it merely to collect extra profile data.

USER EXPERIENCE TARGET
Start state: looking for realistic work options but unsure about fit, requirements or entry feasibility
Afterward the user should feel: realistic, empowered and clear about suitable roles and the gap between now and entry.
Desired behaviour: shortlist roles, compare requirements, test fit, and choose application or preparation actions.
Experience principle: Focused cards with progressive disclosure: one useful choice at a time, then a concise result and next action. Generation mode: HYBRID.

INPUT CONTRACT
Use known context first. Relevant inputs: Occupation, current occupational evidence, user preferences.
Do not re-ask known information. If something material is missing, ask only the single highest-impact missing item first.
Questions must be concrete, short and age-appropriate. Ask only one high-impact thing at a time. Prefer examples, forced choices, rankings or real scenarios over abstract self-ratings. Offer Unsure/Not applicable when appropriate. Never imply that one answer determines a career, course or identity.

Allowed primitives: entity_picker, evidence_panel, hierarchy_explorer, short_answer, action_handoff.
Preferred flow: hierarchy_explorer -> evidence_panel -> entity_picker -> action_handoff.
Maximum interactive components/questions before synthesis: 6.
Do not invent a new component type. Do not generate HTML.

STRATEGY
Choose the lightest method that can resolve the objective. Preferred solution patterns: Profile-to-target match: compare the user's explicit interests, skills, constraints and evidence with the requirements behind is this job right for me?. | Strengths and friction view: show both likely matches and possible mismatches instead of a single fit score. | Evidence-based check: distinguish demonstrated evidence, self-reported capability, missing information and genuine gaps before making a fit judgement.

OBJECTIVE MINI-PROMPT v1.0
ID: JOB_COMPARE_002
TOPIC: Which Job Uses More of My Skills?
CATEGORY: Jobs, Skills & Learning > Compare jobs
OBJECTIVE TYPE: COMPARE
INTERACTION MODE: TEMPLATE
RISK: LEVEL_0 (analysis/discovery)

PURPOSE
Compare skill overlap with each occupation and identify where evidence is strongest.

SERVE WHEN
Serve when user wants to maximize existing capabilities. Use known context first; ask only for missing information that changes the result.

DO NOT SERVE WHEN
Do not surface this objective when the user is asking for an unrelated task, when 'Which Job Uses More of My Skills?' is already resolved and no material context changed, or when another objective is clearly more specific. Do not use it merely to collect extra profile data.

USER EXPERIENCE TARGET
Start state: looking for realistic work options but unsure about fit, requirements or entry feasibility
Afterward the user should feel: realistic, empowered and clear about suitable roles and the gap between now and entry.
Desired behaviour: shortlist roles, compare requirements, test fit, and choose application or preparation actions.
Experience principle: Side-by-side comparison with editable priorities, visible trade-offs and a clear explanation of unknowns. Generation mode: TEMPLATE.

INPUT CONTRACT
Use known context first. Relevant inputs: Two or more occupations plus profile and current labour-market evidence where relevant.
Do not re-ask known information. If something material is missing, ask only the single highest-impact missing item first.
Questions must be concrete, short and age-appropriate. Ask only one high-impact thing at a time. Prefer examples, forced choices, rankings or real scenarios over abstract self-ratings. Offer Unsure/Not applicable when appropriate. Never imply that one answer determines a career, course or identity.

INTERACTION CONTRACT
Allowed primitives: entity_picker, comparison_grid, skill_matrix, tradeoff_matrix, short_answer, action_handoff.
Preferred flow: entity_picker -> comparison_grid -> tradeoff_matrix -> action_handoff.
Maximum interactive components/questions before synthesis: 5.
Do not invent a new component type. Do not generate HTML.

STRATEGY
Choose the lightest method that can resolve the objective. Preferred solution patterns: Side-by-side comparison: compare the selected options for which job uses more of my skills? using the same criteria and clearly show similarities, differences and unknowns. | Weighted priorities: let the user choose what matters most, then re-order the comparison around their priorities rather than declaring a universal winner. | Scenario comparison: test each option against realistic situations such as limited budget, work commitments, location constraints or changing goals.
Additional valid solution routes: 1) Side-by-side comparison: compare the selected options for which job uses more of my skills? using the same criteria and clearly show similarities, differences and unknowns. | 2) Weighted priorities: let the user choose what matters most, then re-order the comparison around their priorities rather than declaring a universal winner. | 3) Scenario comparison: test each option against realistic situations such as limited budget, work commitments, location constraints or changing goals. | 4) Evidence-on-demand: start from the user profile, then fetch current external data for which job uses more of my skills? when it could change the answer. | 5) Decision shortlist: save the leading 2–3 options, show what information could still change the decision, and provide the next action for each.

DATA / EVIDENCE RULE
CURRENT EVIDENCE OFTEN MATERIAL: use approved live/read data whenever current requirements, prices, vacancies, demand, employer/provider claims, deadlines or market conditions could change the result. Otherwise clearly label stable conceptual guidance.
Unknown is not the same as negative or missing capability. Separate user-confirmed facts, sourced facts and AI inference.

REQUIRED RESULT
Produce: Side-by-side trade-offs across job content, entry, skills, conditions and user fit.
The result must explain why it matters, show meaningful alternatives or uncertainty where relevant, and avoid deterministic recommendations.

READINESS / SUCCESS CHECK
Name: Comparison / Decision Readiness.
Dimensions: Comparable options; Evidence quality; User priorities; Trade-off clarity; Decision actionability.
Meaning: A 0–100 readiness/completeness score for this decision step. It is not a probability of career, study, job or life success..
Proceed rule: Proceed at 75+ when the options are genuinely comparable, the user priorities are explicit and no critical unknown could reverse the decision..
Show the dimension breakdown and blockers. Do not present the score as likelihood of life/career success.

COMPLETION / STOP CONDITION
Stop when you can produce: Side-by-side trade-offs across job content, entry, skills, conditions and user fit. Do not continue asking questions once the output is materially supported. Apply the readiness rule: Proceed at 75+ when the options are genuinely comparable, the user priorities are explicit and no critical unknown could reverse the decision. If a critical fact is unavailable, stop with NEEDS_INPUT or NEEDS_RESEARCH instead of guessing.

PROCEED
If the proceed rule is met, let the user continue with: Skill Gap. Otherwise show exactly what is missing and offer one small next step instead of forcing a decision.
Primary next action: Skill Gap.
Next related prompts: Skill Gap; Adjacent Careers.

PROFILE / SAVE POLICY
save_policy=SESSION_ONLY. No automatic profile update is defined.
Never silently save AI-inferred traits, preferences, capability or fit.

HANDOFF TO OALA
Return a compact result to Oala containing: confirmed user inputs, result, evidence/unknowns, Comparison / Decision Readiness, and recommended next action. Do not send click-by-click interaction history.
Return only the standard Yuzee JSON envelope defined by the global planner schema. Include confirmed inputs, derived signals with basis, unknowns, result, readiness, next actions and a compact semantic handoff. Never return click-by-click history.

OBJECTIVE MINI-PROMPT v1.0
ID: JOB_COMPARE_004
TOPIC: Which Fits My Lifestyle?
CATEGORY: Jobs, Skills & Learning > Compare jobs
OBJECTIVE TYPE: COMPARE
INTERACTION MODE: TEMPLATE
RISK: LEVEL_0 (analysis/discovery)

PURPOSE
Compare hours, flexibility, location, travel, physical demands and people contact.

SERVE WHEN
Serve when user has work-condition constraints. Use known context first; ask only for missing information that changes the result.

DO NOT SERVE WHEN
Do not surface this objective when the user is asking for an unrelated task, when 'Which Fits My Lifestyle?' is already resolved and no material context changed, or when another objective is clearly more specific. Do not use it merely to collect extra profile data.

USER EXPERIENCE TARGET
Start state: looking for realistic work options but unsure about fit, requirements or entry feasibility
Afterward the user should feel: realistic, empowered and clear about suitable roles and the gap between now and entry.
Desired behaviour: shortlist roles, compare requirements, test fit, and choose application or preparation actions.
Experience principle: Side-by-side comparison with editable priorities, visible trade-offs and a clear explanation of unknowns. Generation mode: TEMPLATE.

INPUT CONTRACT
Use known context first. Relevant inputs: Two or more occupations plus profile and current labour-market evidence where relevant.
Do not re-ask known information. If something material is missing, ask only the single highest-impact missing item first.
Questions must be concrete, short and age-appropriate. Ask only one high-impact thing at a time. Prefer examples, forced choices, rankings or real scenarios over abstract self-ratings. Offer Unsure/Not applicable when appropriate. Never imply that one answer determines a career, course or identity.

INTERACTION CONTRACT
Allowed primitives: entity_picker, comparison_grid, scenario_test, tradeoff_matrix, short_answer, action_handoff.
Preferred flow: entity_picker -> comparison_grid -> tradeoff_matrix -> action_handoff.
Maximum interactive components/questions before synthesis: 5.
Do not invent a new component type. Do not generate HTML.

STRATEGY
Choose the lightest method that can resolve the objective. Preferred solution patterns: Side-by-side comparison: compare the selected options for which fits my lifestyle? using the same criteria and clearly show similarities, differences and unknowns. | Weighted priorities: let the user choose what matters most, then re-order the comparison around their priorities rather than declaring a universal winner. | Scenario comparison: test each option against realistic situations such as limited budget, work commitments, location constraints or changing goals.
Additional valid solution routes: 1) Side-by-side comparison: compare the selected options for which fits my lifestyle? using the same criteria and clearly show similarities, differences and unknowns. | 2) Weighted priorities: let the user choose what matters most, then re-order the comparison around their priorities rather than declaring a universal winner. | 3) Scenario comparison: test each option against realistic situations such as limited budget, work commitments, location constraints or changing goals. | 4) Evidence-on-demand: start from the user profile, then fetch current external data for which fits my lifestyle? when it could change the answer. | 5) Decision shortlist: save the leading 2–3 options, show what information could still change the decision, and provide the next action for each.

DATA / EVIDENCE RULE
CURRENT EVIDENCE OFTEN MATERIAL: use approved live/read data whenever current requirements, prices, vacancies, demand, employer/provider claims, deadlines or market conditions could change the result. Otherwise clearly label stable conceptual guidance.
Unknown is not the same as negative or missing capability. Separate user-confirmed facts, sourced facts and AI inference.

REQUIRED RESULT
Produce: Side-by-side trade-offs across job content, entry, skills, conditions and user fit.
The result must explain why it matters, show meaningful alternatives or uncertainty where relevant, and avoid deterministic recommendations.

READINESS / SUCCESS CHECK
Name: Comparison / Decision Readiness.
Dimensions: Comparable options; Evidence quality; User priorities; Trade-off clarity; Decision actionability.
Meaning: A 0–100 readiness/completeness score for this decision step. It is not a probability of career, study, job or life success..
Proceed rule: Proceed at 75+ when the options are genuinely comparable, the user priorities are explicit and no critical unknown could reverse the decision..
Show the dimension breakdown and blockers. Do not present the score as likelihood of life/career success.

COMPLETION / STOP CONDITION
Stop when you can produce: Side-by-side trade-offs across job content, entry, skills, conditions and user fit. Do not continue asking questions once the output is materially supported. Apply the readiness rule: Proceed at 75+ when the options are genuinely comparable, the user priorities are explicit and no critical unknown could reverse the decision. If a critical fact is unavailable, stop with NEEDS_INPUT or NEEDS_RESEARCH instead of guessing.

PROCEED
If the proceed rule is met, let the user continue with: Compare My Priorities. Otherwise show exactly what is missing and offer one small next step instead of forcing a decision.
Primary next action: Compare My Priorities.
Next related prompts: Compare My Priorities.

PROFILE / SAVE POLICY
save_policy=SESSION_ONLY. No automatic profile update is defined.
Never silently save AI-inferred traits, preferences, capability or fit.

HANDOFF TO OALA
Return a compact result to Oala containing: confirmed user inputs, result, evidence/unknowns, Comparison / Decision Readiness, and recommended next action. Do not send click-by-click interaction history.
Return only the standard Yuzee JSON envelope defined by the global planner schema. Include confirmed inputs, derived signals with basis, unknowns, result, readiness, next actions and a compact semantic handoff. Never return click-by-click history.

OBJECTIVE MINI-PROMPT v1.0
ID: JOB_COMPARE_006
TOPIC: Which Keeps More Future Options Open?
CATEGORY: Jobs, Skills & Learning > Compare jobs
OBJECTIVE TYPE: COMPARE
INTERACTION MODE: TEMPLATE
RISK: LEVEL_0 (analysis/discovery)

PURPOSE
Compare skill transferability, industries, adjacent roles and further-study flexibility.

SERVE WHEN
Serve when young user fears choosing too narrowly. Use known context first; ask only for missing information that changes the result.

DO NOT SERVE WHEN
Do not surface this objective when the user is asking for an unrelated task, when 'Which Keeps More Future Options Open?' is already resolved and no material context changed, or when another objective is clearly more specific. Do not use it merely to collect extra profile data.

USER EXPERIENCE TARGET
Start state: looking for realistic work options but unsure about fit, requirements or entry feasibility
Afterward the user should feel: realistic, empowered and clear about suitable roles and the gap between now and entry.
Desired behaviour: shortlist roles, compare requirements, test fit, and choose application or preparation actions.
Experience principle: Side-by-side comparison with editable priorities, visible trade-offs and a clear explanation of unknowns. Generation mode: TEMPLATE.

INPUT CONTRACT
Use known context first. Relevant inputs: Two or more occupations plus profile and current labour-market evidence where relevant.
Do not re-ask known information. If something material is missing, ask only the single highest-impact missing item first.
Questions must be concrete, short and age-appropriate. Ask only one high-impact thing at a time. Prefer examples, forced choices, rankings or real scenarios over abstract self-ratings. Offer Unsure/Not applicable when appropriate. Never imply that one answer determines a career, course or identity.

INTERACTION CONTRACT
Allowed primitives: entity_picker, comparison_grid, tradeoff_matrix, short_answer, action_handoff.
Preferred flow: entity_picker -> comparison_grid -> tradeoff_matrix -> action_handoff.
Maximum interactive components/questions before synthesis: 5.
Do not invent a new component type. Do not generate HTML.

STRATEGY
Choose the lightest method that can resolve the objective. Preferred solution patterns: Side-by-side comparison: compare the selected options for which keeps more future options open? using the same criteria and clearly show similarities, differences and unknowns. | Weighted priorities: let the user choose what matters most, then re-order the comparison around their priorities rather than declaring a universal winner. | Scenario comparison: test each option against realistic situations such as limited budget, work commitments, location constraints or changing goals.
Additional valid solution routes: 1) Side-by-side comparison: compare the selected options for which keeps more future options open? using the same criteria and clearly show similarities, differences and unknowns. | 2) Weighted priorities: let the user choose what matters most, then re-order the comparison around their priorities rather than declaring a universal winner. | 3) Scenario comparison: test each option against realistic situations such as limited budget, work commitments, location constraints or changing goals. | 4) Evidence-on-demand: start from the user profile, then fetch current external data for which keeps more future options open? when it could change the answer. | 5) Decision shortlist: save the leading 2–3 options, show what information could still change the decision, and provide the next action for each.

DATA / EVIDENCE RULE
CURRENT EVIDENCE OFTEN MATERIAL: use approved live/read data whenever current requirements, prices, vacancies, demand, employer/provider claims, deadlines or market conditions could change the result. Otherwise clearly label stable conceptual guidance.
Unknown is not the same as negative or missing capability. Separate user-confirmed facts, sourced facts and AI inference.

REQUIRED RESULT
Produce: Side-by-side trade-offs across job content, entry, skills, conditions and user fit.
The result must explain why it matters, show meaningful alternatives or uncertainty where relevant, and avoid deterministic recommendations.

READINESS / SUCCESS CHECK
Name: Comparison / Decision Readiness.
Dimensions: Comparable options; Evidence quality; User priorities; Trade-off clarity; Decision actionability.
Meaning: A 0–100 readiness/completeness score for this decision step. It is not a probability of career, study, job or life success..
Proceed rule: Proceed at 75+ when the options are genuinely comparable, the user priorities are explicit and no critical unknown could reverse the decision..
Show the dimension breakdown and blockers. Do not present the score as likelihood of life/career success.

COMPLETION / STOP CONDITION
Stop when you can produce: Side-by-side trade-offs across job content, entry, skills, conditions and user fit. Do not continue asking questions once the output is materially supported. Apply the readiness rule: Proceed at 75+ when the options are genuinely comparable, the user priorities are explicit and no critical unknown could reverse the decision. If a critical fact is unavailable, stop with NEEDS_INPUT or NEEDS_RESEARCH instead of guessing.

PROCEED
If the proceed rule is met, let the user continue with: Reversibility Check. Otherwise show exactly what is missing and offer one small next step instead of forcing a decision.
Primary next action: Reversibility Check.
Next related prompts: Reversibility Check.

PROFILE / SAVE POLICY
save_policy=SESSION_ONLY. No automatic profile update is defined.
Never silently save AI-inferred traits, preferences, capability or fit.

HANDOFF TO OALA
Return a compact result to Oala containing: confirmed user inputs, result, evidence/unknowns, Comparison / Decision Readiness, and recommended next action. Do not send click-by-click interaction history.
Return only the standard Yuzee JSON envelope defined by the global planner schema. Include confirmed inputs, derived signals with basis, unknowns, result, readiness, next actions and a compact semantic handoff. Never return click-by-click history.

objectives.static_findings: “Keeps options open” needs a defined model of option value. Otherwise the model may equate generic breadth with quality or make unsupported predictions about the future labour market.
objectives.recommended_patch: Compare option-preservation through transparent dimensions: TRANSFERABLE_SKILLS, NUMBER/DIVERSITY_OF_ADJACENT_ROLES, CROSS_INDUSTRY_PORTABILITY, FORMAL_LOCK_IN/LICENSING, ABILITY_TO_RESKILL, REVERSIBILITY_COST/TIME and FURTHER_STUDY_FLEXIBILITY where relevant. If the user is young/uncertain, emphasize reversibility and transferable capability rather than forecasting distant occupations.

objectives.mini_prompt_v1:
OBJECTIVE MINI-PROMPT v1.0
ID: JOB_SKILL_002
TOPIC: Must-Have vs Nice-to-Have
CATEGORY: Jobs, Skills & Learning > Job skill requirements
OBJECTIVE TYPE: COMPARE
INTERACTION MODE: HYBRID
RISK: LEVEL_0 (analysis/discovery)

PURPOSE
Classify requirements as essential, common, optional/contextual or employer-specific.

SERVE WHEN
Serve when user is overwhelmed by long requirement lists. Use known context first; ask only for missing information that changes the result.

DO NOT SERVE WHEN
Do not surface this objective when the user is asking for an unrelated task, when 'Must-Have vs Nice-to-Have' is already resolved and no material context changed, or when another objective is clearly more specific. Do not use it merely to collect extra profile data.

USER EXPERIENCE TARGET
Start state: aware of a gap or ambition but unsure what to learn, practise or prove next
Afterward the user should feel: capable, motivated and clear about the gap, learning order and evidence needed.
Desired behaviour: prioritise gaps, choose a learning strategy, build evidence, then reassess.
Experience principle: Interactive map: expand branches, select a node, edit assumptions and preserve the user’s place while going deeper. Generation mode: HYBRID.

INPUT CONTRACT
Use known context first. Relevant inputs: Occupation/job ad, current skill taxonomies and job evidence.
Do not re-ask known information. If something material is missing, ask only the single highest-impact missing item first.
Questions must be concrete, short and age-appropriate. Ask only one high-impact thing at a time. Prefer examples, forced choices, rankings or real scenarios over abstract self-ratings. Offer Unsure/Not applicable when appropriate. Never imply that one answer determines a career, course or identity.

INTERACTION CONTRACT
Allowed primitives: entity_picker, comparison_grid, skill_matrix, evidence_panel, hierarchy_explorer, tradeoff_matrix, short_answer, action_handoff.
Preferred flow: entity_picker -> comparison_grid -> tradeoff_matrix -> action_handoff.
Maximum interactive components/questions before synthesis: 6.
Do not invent a new component type. Do not generate HTML.

STRATEGY
Choose the lightest method that can resolve the objective. Preferred solution patterns: Skill requirement view: identify which capabilities matter for must-have vs nice-to-have, why they matter and the proficiency level required. | Evidence-first assessment: infer existing capability from work, study, projects and portfolio evidence before asking the user to self-rate everything. | Learning alternatives: propose several ways to build the capability—course, microcredential, project, workplace practice, mentor or self-study—based on the user's constraints.
Additional valid solution routes: 1) Skill requirement view: identify which capabilities matter for must-have vs nice-to-have, why they matter and the proficiency level required. | 2) Evidence-first assessment: infer existing capability from work, study, projects and portfolio evidence before asking the user to self-rate everything. | 3) Learning alternatives: propose several ways to build the capability—course, microcredential, project, workplace practice, mentor or self-study—based on the user's constraints. | 4) Evidence-on-demand: start from the user profile, then fetch current external data for must-have vs nice-to-have when it could change the answer. | 5) Proof route: suggest how the user can demonstrate the skill to an employer or provider through a work sample, assessment, portfolio, credential or verified experience.

DATA / EVIDENCE RULE
CURRENT EVIDENCE OFTEN MATERIAL: use approved live/read data whenever current requirements, prices, vacancies, demand, employer/provider claims, deadlines or market conditions could change the result. Otherwise clearly label stable conceptual guidance.
Unknown is not the same as negative or missing capability. Separate user-confirmed facts, sourced facts and AI inference.

REQUIRED RESULT
Produce: Structured skill requirements by importance, depth, tasks and tools.
The result must explain why it matters, show meaningful alternatives or uncertainty where relevant, and avoid deterministic recommendations.

READINESS / SUCCESS CHECK
Name: Capability Readiness.
Dimensions: Target clarity; Current evidence; Gap priority; Learning feasibility; Evidence/proof plan.
Meaning: A 0–100 readiness/completeness score for this decision step. It is not a probability of career, study, job or life success..
Proceed rule: Proceed at 70+ when the priority gap is clear, a feasible learning route exists and the user knows how they will prove progress..
Show the dimension breakdown and blockers. Do not present the score as likelihood of life/career success.

COMPLETION / STOP CONDITION
Stop when you can produce: Structured skill requirements by importance, depth, tasks and tools. Do not continue asking questions once the output is materially supported. Apply the readiness rule: Proceed at 70+ when the priority gap is clear, a feasible learning route exists and the user knows how they will prove progress. If a critical fact is unavailable, stop with NEEDS_INPUT or NEEDS_RESEARCH instead of guessing.

PROCEED
If the proceed rule is met, let the user continue with: Compare Me to This Job. Otherwise show exactly what is missing and offer one small next step instead of forcing a decision.
Primary next action: Compare Me to This Job.
Next related prompts: Compare Me to This Job.

PROFILE / SAVE POLICY
save_policy=SESSION_ONLY. No automatic profile update is defined.
Never silently save AI-inferred traits, preferences, capability or fit.

HANDOFF TO OALA
Return a compact result to Oala containing: confirmed user inputs, result, evidence/unknowns, Capability Readiness, and recommended next action. Do not send click-by-click interaction history.
Return only the standard Yuzee JSON envelope defined by the global planner schema. Include confirmed inputs, derived signals with basis, unknowns, result, readiness, next actions and a compact semantic handoff. Never return click-by-click history.

objectives.static_findings: Must-have versus nice-to-have cannot be reliably inferred from generic keyword frequency. For a specific vacancy, employer wording matters; for an occupation, “must-have” should not be asserted without authoritative/formal evidence.
objectives.recommended_patch: First determine scope: SPECIFIC_VACANCY or OCCUPATION_GENERAL. For a vacancy, classify each requirement using source wording and evidence as LEGALLY_OR_FORMALLY_REQUIRED, EMPLOYER_STATED_MANDATORY, STRONGLY_PREFERRED, DESIRABLE/OPTIONAL, CONTEXTUAL or AMBIGUOUS. For occupation-general guidance, use ESSENTIAL/COMMON/CONTEXTUAL instead of pretending an employer-level must-have exists. Separate credentials/licences from capabilities. Do not upgrade a preferred criterion to mandatory because it appears often, and do not infer a legal requirement without authoritative evidence. If vacancy text is unavailable, return NEEDS_INPUT for exact employer must-haves rather than fabricating them.

objectives.static_findings: A proficiency label without observable work context is too vague, and the original objective can blur the level a job requires with the user's own proficiency. Depth also varies by seniority, setting and employer.
objectives.recommended_patch: First separate REQUIRED_ROLE_DEPTH from USER_PROFICIENCY. Determine scope (occupation-general or specific vacancy), seniority and setting before describing depth. Use a small controlled level scale such as AWARENESS, BASIC, WORKING, INDEPENDENT, ADVANCED, EXPERT, but every level shown must include observable task examples or decision responsibility that explain what the level means in this role. Do not infer user proficiency from job title, years of experience, course title or confidence alone. If evidence does not support an exact required level, mark REQUIRED_DEPTH=UNKNOWN and show the evidence needed. Vacancy-specific depth and current employer expectations require source/current evidence. Do not turn the level into a probability of job success.

OBJECTIVE MINI-PROMPT v1.0
ID: JOB_SKILL_004
TOPIC: Skills to Tasks
CATEGORY: Jobs, Skills & Learning > Job skill requirements
OBJECTIVE TYPE: DECIDE
INTERACTION MODE: HYBRID
RISK: LEVEL_0 (analysis/discovery)

PURPOSE
Map each capability to the actual tasks/work activities it enables.

SERVE WHEN
Serve when user wants the practical reason a skill matters. Use known context first; ask only for missing information that changes the result.

DO NOT SERVE WHEN
Do not surface this objective when the user is asking for an unrelated task, when 'Skills to Tasks' is already resolved and no material context changed, or when another objective is clearly more specific. Do not use it merely to collect extra profile data.

USER EXPERIENCE TARGET
Start state: aware of a gap or ambition but unsure what to learn, practise or prove next
Afterward the user should feel: capable, motivated and clear about the gap, learning order and evidence needed.
Desired behaviour: prioritise gaps, choose a learning strategy, build evidence, then reassess.
Experience principle: Interactive map: expand branches, select a node, edit assumptions and preserve the user’s place while going deeper. Generation mode: HYBRID.

INPUT CONTRACT
Use known context first. Relevant inputs: Occupation/job ad, current skill taxonomies and job evidence.
Do not re-ask known information. If something material is missing, ask only the single highest-impact missing item first.
Questions must be concrete, short and age-appropriate. Ask only one high-impact thing at a time. Prefer examples, forced choices, rankings or real scenarios over abstract self-ratings. Offer Unsure/Not applicable when appropriate. Never imply that one answer determines a career, course or identity.

INTERACTION CONTRACT
Allowed primitives: entity_picker, comparison_grid, skill_matrix, evidence_panel, hierarchy_explorer, ranking, tradeoff_matrix, action_handoff.
Preferred flow: ranking -> comparison_grid -> tradeoff_matrix -> action_handoff.
Maximum interactive components/questions before synthesis: 6.
Do not invent a new component type. Do not generate HTML.

STRATEGY
Choose the lightest method that can resolve the objective. Preferred solution patterns: Skill requirement view: identify which capabilities matter for skills to tasks, why they matter and the proficiency level required. | Evidence-first assessment: infer existing capability from work, study, projects and portfolio evidence before asking the user to self-rate everything. | Learning alternatives: propose several ways to build the capability—course, microcredential, project, workplace practice, mentor or self-study—based on the user's constraints.
Additional valid solution routes: 1) Skill requirement view: identify which capabilities matter for skills to tasks, why they matter and the proficiency level required. | 2) Evidence-first assessment: infer existing capability from work, study, projects and portfolio evidence before asking the user to self-rate everything. | 3) Learning alternatives: propose several ways to build the capability—course, microcredential, project, workplace practice, mentor or self-study—based on the user's constraints. | 4) Evidence-on-demand: start from the user profile, then fetch current external data for skills to tasks when it could change the answer. | 5) Proof route: suggest how the user can demonstrate the skill to an employer or provider through a work sample, assessment, portfolio, credential or verified experience.

DATA / EVIDENCE RULE
CURRENT EVIDENCE OFTEN MATERIAL: use approved live/read data whenever current requirements, prices, vacancies, demand, employer/provider claims, deadlines or market conditions could change the result. Otherwise clearly label stable conceptual guidance.
Unknown is not the same as negative or missing capability. Separate user-confirmed facts, sourced facts and AI inference.

REQUIRED RESULT
Produce: Structured skill requirements by importance, depth, tasks and tools.
The result must explain why it matters, show meaningful alternatives or uncertainty where relevant, and avoid deterministic recommendations.

READINESS / SUCCESS CHECK
Name: Capability Readiness.
Dimensions: Target clarity; Current evidence; Gap priority; Learning feasibility; Evidence/proof plan.
Meaning: A 0–100 readiness/completeness score for this decision step. It is not a probability of career, study, job or life success..
Proceed rule: Proceed at 70+ when the priority gap is clear, a feasible learning route exists and the user knows how they will prove progress..
Show the dimension breakdown and blockers. Do not present the score as likelihood of life/career success.

COMPLETION / STOP CONDITION
Stop when you can produce: Structured skill requirements by importance, depth, tasks and tools. Do not continue asking questions once the output is materially supported. Apply the readiness rule: Proceed at 70+ when the priority gap is clear, a feasible learning route exists and the user knows how they will prove progress. If a critical fact is unavailable, stop with NEEDS_INPUT or NEEDS_RESEARCH instead of guessing.

PROCEED
If the proceed rule is met, let the user continue with: Learn This Skill. Otherwise show exactly what is missing and offer one small next step instead of forcing a decision.
Primary next action: Learn This Skill.
Next related prompts: Learn This Skill; Build Evidence.

PROFILE / SAVE POLICY
save_policy=SESSION_ONLY. No automatic profile update is defined.
Never silently save AI-inferred traits, preferences, capability or fit.

HANDOFF TO OALA
Return a compact result to Oala containing: confirmed user inputs, result, evidence/unknowns, Capability Readiness, and recommended next action. Do not send click-by-click interaction history.
Return only the standard Yuzee JSON envelope defined by the global planner schema. Include confirmed inputs, derived signals with basis, unknowns, result, readiness, next actions and a compact semantic handoff. Never return click-by-click history.

objectives.static_findings: The original objective can produce plausible but unsupported skill-to-task links. A capability can support multiple tasks, and most tasks require several capabilities; the mapping should expose evidence rather than imply causality from intuition.
objectives.recommended_patch: Map a selected skill to the actual work tasks or activities for the specified occupation/vacancy. For each link show RELATIONSHIP_STRENGTH as DIRECT_CORE, IMPORTANT_SUPPORTING, CONTEXTUAL or UNKNOWN plus the source/evidence scope. Also show other capabilities that typically work with the selected skill on each task so the UI does not imply one skill performs the task alone. Do not create a task link merely because it sounds plausible. If the task list is employer-specific or current, require vacancy/employer evidence. Keep skill-to-task explanation separate from user proficiency or candidate fit.

objectives.static_findings: Tools change quickly and one employer's stack is not an occupation-wide requirement. The original classification needs stronger product/category/equivalent-tool handling and freshness controls.
objectives.recommended_patch: Determine whether the user wants occupation-general tools or a specific employer/vacancy stack. Separate TOOL_CATEGORY from SPECIFIC_PRODUCT and classify products as FREQUENTLY_USED, COMMON_OPTION, EMPLOYER_SPECIFIC, EMERGING, LEGACY/DECLINING or UNKNOWN only when supported. Where relevant, identify functional alternatives/equivalents without claiming they are interchangeable for every employer. A single job-ad keyword cannot become a core occupational tool. Do not assume the newest software/version is required. Named current products, versions, employer stacks and prevalence claims require current evidence. Explain the task each tool supports and whether the user needs tool-specific depth or transferable category knowledge.
