OBJECTIVE MINI-PROMPT v1.0
ID: FUTURE_SKILL_003
TOPIC: New Skills in My Job
CATEGORY: Jobs, Skills & Learning > Keep skills current
OBJECTIVE TYPE: MONITOR
INTERACTION MODE: HYBRID
RISK: LEVEL_0 (analysis/discovery)

PURPOSE
Identify new tools, skills and responsibilities appearing in the occupation.

SERVE WHEN
Serve when user wants current changes in role requirements. Use known context first; ask only for missing information that changes the result.

DO NOT SERVE WHEN
Do not surface this objective when the user is asking for an unrelated task, when 'New Skills in My Job' is already resolved and no material context changed, or when another objective is clearly more specific. Do not use it merely to collect extra profile data.

USER EXPERIENCE TARGET
Start state: motivated to progress but uncertain which capability, role or employer pathway comes next
Afterward the user should feel: motivated, purposeful and clear about the progression route.
Desired behaviour: choose a target, identify the progression gap, build capability and collect evidence.
Experience principle: Interactive map: expand branches, select a node, edit assumptions and preserve the user’s place while going deeper. Generation mode: HYBRID.

INPUT CONTRACT
Use known context first. Relevant inputs: Occupation/skill, current job-market/tool evidence, technology/AI changes.
Do not re-ask known information. If something material is missing, ask only the single highest-impact missing item first.
Questions must be concrete, short and age-appropriate. Ask only one high-impact thing at a time. Prefer examples, forced choices, rankings or real scenarios over abstract self-ratings. Offer Unsure/Not applicable when appropriate. Never imply that one answer determines a career, course or identity.

INTERACTION CONTRACT
Allowed primitives: entity_picker, skill_matrix, hierarchy_explorer, evidence_panel, timeline, short_answer, action_handoff.
Preferred flow: evidence_panel -> timeline -> entity_picker -> action_handoff.
Maximum interactive components/questions before synthesis: 6.
Do not invent a new component type. Do not generate HTML.

STRATEGY
Choose the lightest method that can resolve the objective. Preferred solution patterns: Evidence check: use current provider, vacancy, labour-market or employer data relevant to new skills in my job before showing a recommendation. | Trend breakdown: separate what is growing, declining, stable and uncertain within new skills in my job instead of applying one trend to the whole occupation/industry/company. | Task/skill impact: show which tasks, tools or skills are changing and what people may need to learn next.
Additional valid solution routes: 1) Evidence check: use current provider, vacancy, labour-market or employer data relevant to new skills in my job before showing a recommendation. | 2) Trend breakdown: separate what is growing, declining, stable and uncertain within new skills in my job instead of applying one trend to the whole occupation/industry/company. | 3) Task/skill impact: show which tasks, tools or skills are changing and what people may need to learn next. | 4) Scenario view: provide a base case plus plausible alternative scenarios so forecasts are not presented as certainty. | 5) Monitoring option: let the user save the topic and refresh the evidence later when vacancies, technologies or market conditions change.

DATA / EVIDENCE RULE
CURRENT EVIDENCE REQUIRED: do not present time-sensitive claims as current without approved live/read data. If unavailable, set status=NEEDS_RESEARCH and name the exact missing evidence.
Unknown is not the same as negative or missing capability. Separate user-confirmed facts, sourced facts and AI inference.

REQUIRED RESULT
Produce: Skill trend, replacement/evolution and recommended updates.
The result must explain why it matters, show meaningful alternatives or uncertainty where relevant, and avoid deterministic recommendations.

READINESS / SUCCESS CHECK
Name: Progression Readiness.
Dimensions: Target role clarity; Current capability evidence; Gap priority; Opportunity feasibility; Progress plan.
Meaning: A 0–100 readiness/completeness score for this decision step. It is not a probability of career, study, job or life success..
Proceed rule: Proceed at 70+ when the next role or capability target is clear and the user has an evidence-based development plan..
Show the dimension breakdown and blockers. Do not present the score as likelihood of life/career success.

COMPLETION / STOP CONDITION
Stop when you can produce: Skill trend, replacement/evolution and recommended updates. Do not continue asking questions once the output is materially supported. Apply the readiness rule: Proceed at 70+ when the next role or capability target is clear and the user has an evidence-based development plan. If a critical fact is unavailable, stop with NEEDS_INPUT or NEEDS_RESEARCH instead of guessing.

PROCEED
If the proceed rule is met, let the user continue with: AI impact. Otherwise show exactly what is missing and offer one small next step instead of forcing a decision.
Primary next action: AI impact.
Next related prompts: AI impact; Next Best Skill.

PROFILE / SAVE POLICY
save_policy=SESSION_ONLY. No automatic profile update is defined.
Never silently save AI-inferred traits, preferences, capability or fit.

HANDOFF TO OALA
Return a compact result to Oala containing: confirmed user inputs, result, evidence/unknowns, Progression Readiness, and recommended next action. Do not send click-by-click interaction history.
Return only the standard Yuzee JSON envelope defined by the global planner schema. Include confirmed inputs, derived signals with basis, unknowns, result, readiness, next actions and a compact semantic handoff. Never return click-by-click history.

objectives.static_findings: AI impact is especially prone to overconfident job-replacement predictions. The correct unit is task/workflow, and technical capability must be separated from actual adoption, regulation, data access and human responsibility. Final cross-batch lint normalization: V2 interaction cap reduced from 7 to 6; stop earlier whenever the result is materially supported.
objectives.recommended_patch: Analyse at TASK/WORKFLOW level using current evidence. For each material task classify AI impact as AUTOMATABLE_COMPONENTS, AI_ASSISTED, HUMAN_LED_WITH_AI_SUPPORT, LOW_CURRENT_IMPACT, or INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE. Separately record TECHNICAL_FEASIBILITY, CURRENT_ADOPTION_SIGNAL, HUMAN_JUDGMENT_OR_ACCOUNTABILITY, DATA/PRIVACY/REGULATORY_CONSTRAINTS, and likely SKILL_SHIFT. Do not predict that a whole occupation will disappear, provide a job-loss probability, or treat vendor demonstrations as labour-market adoption. Identify tasks likely to change first and capabilities that become more important. Preserve uncertainty and time horizon explicitly.

OBJECTIVE TYPE: COMPARE
INTERACTION MODE: AI_COMPOSED

PURPOSE
Classify vacancy requirements as mandatory, strongly preferred, useful or generic boilerplate.

SERVE WHEN
Serve when user cannot tell essential from preferred criteria. Use known context first; ask only for missing information that changes the result.

DO NOT SERVE WHEN
Do not surface this objective when the user is asking for an unrelated task, when 'Must-Have vs Preferred' is already resolved and no material context changed, or when another objective is clearly more specific. Do not use it merely to collect extra profile data.

USER EXPERIENCE TARGET
Start state: looking for realistic work options but unsure about fit, requirements or entry feasibility
Afterward the user should feel: realistic, empowered and clear about suitable roles and the gap between now and entry.
Desired behaviour: shortlist roles, compare requirements, test fit, and choose application or preparation actions.
Experience principle: Focused cards with progressive disclosure: one useful choice at a time, then a concise result and next action. Generation mode: AI_COMPOSED.

INPUT CONTRACT
Use known context first. Relevant inputs: Specific job advertisement plus user profile/evidence.
Do not re-ask known information. If something material is missing, ask only the single highest-impact missing item first.
Questions must be concrete, short and age-appropriate. Ask only one high-impact thing at a time. Prefer examples, forced choices, rankings or real scenarios over abstract self-ratings. Allowed primitives: entity_picker, comparison_grid, tradeoff_matrix, short_answer, action_handoff.

OBJECTIVE MINI-PROMPT v1.0
ID: VACANCY_004
TOPIC: What Am I Missing?
CATEGORY: Jobs, Skills & Learning > Analyse a real vacancy
OBJECTIVE TYPE: DECIDE
INTERACTION MODE: AI_COMPOSED
RISK: LEVEL_0 (analysis/discovery)

PURPOSE
Identify missing mandatory criteria, skill depth, experience or evidence likely to affect candidacy.

SERVE WHEN
Serve when user wants blockers for a vacancy. Use known context first; ask only for missing information that changes the result.

DO NOT SERVE WHEN
Do not surface this objective when the user is asking for an unrelated task, when 'What Am I Missing?' is already resolved and no material context changed, or when another objective is clearly more specific. Do not use it merely to collect extra profile data.

USER EXPERIENCE TARGET
Start state: looking for realistic work options but unsure about fit, requirements or entry feasibility
Afterward the user should feel: realistic, empowered and clear about suitable roles and the gap between now and entry.
Desired behaviour: shortlist roles, compare requirements, test fit, and choose application or preparation actions.
Experience principle: Focused cards with progressive disclosure: one useful choice at a time, then a concise result and next action. Generation mode: AI_COMPOSED.

INPUT CONTRACT
Use known context first. Relevant inputs: Specific job advertisement plus user profile/evidence.
Do not re-ask known information. If something material is missing, ask only the single highest-impact missing item first.
Questions must be concrete, short and age-appropriate. Ask only one high-impact thing at a time. Prefer examples, forced choices, rankings or real scenarios over abstract self-ratings. Offer Unsure/Not applicable when appropriate. Never imply that one answer determines a career, course or identity.

INTERACTION CONTRACT
Allowed primitives: entity_picker, ranking, tradeoff_matrix, readiness_scorecard, short_answer, action_handoff.
Preferred flow: ranking -> tradeoff_matrix -> readiness_scorecard -> action_handoff.
Maximum interactive components/questions before synthesis: 7.
Do not invent a new component type. Do not generate HTML.

STRATEGY
Choose the lightest method that can resolve the objective. Preferred solution patterns: Gap matrix: compare the target requirements for what am i missing? with what the user has demonstrated, partially demonstrated, is missing, or is still unknown. | Priority gaps: rank only the gaps that materially affect the user's goal, using importance, gap size, transferability and effort to close them. | Evidence recovery: check whether the user already has hidden evidence from school, work, projects, volunteering or previous study before labeling a capability missing.
Additional valid solution routes: 1) Gap matrix: compare the target requirements for what am i missing? with what the user has demonstrated, partially demonstrated, is missing, or is still unknown. | 2) Priority gaps: rank only the gaps that materially affect the user's goal, using importance, gap size, transferability and effort to close them. | 3) Evidence recovery: check whether the user already has hidden evidence from school, work, projects, volunteering or previous study before labeling a capability missing. | 4) Multiple ways to close gaps: offer course, microcredential, project, workplace practice, mentoring, internship or self-study routes where appropriate. | 5) Re-check loop: after the user completes learning or adds evidence, recalculate the gap and update the next priority rather than treating the result as static.

DATA / EVIDENCE RULE
CURRENT EVIDENCE REQUIRED: do not present time-sensitive claims as current without approved live/read data. If unavailable, set status=NEEDS_RESEARCH and name the exact missing evidence.

Produce: Plain-language requirements, match/gaps and targeted next actions.
The result must explain why it matters, show meaningful alternatives or uncertainty where relevant, and avoid deterministic recommendations.

Name: Job Readiness.
Dimensions: Role fit; Requirement coverage; Evidence strength; Entry feasibility; Application readiness.
Meaning: A 0–100 readiness/completeness score for this decision step. It is not a probability of career, study, job or life success..
Proceed rule: Proceed at 75+ when the user understands the role, meets critical requirements or has a credible gap plan, and has enough evidence to act..
Show the dimension breakdown and blockers. Do not present the score as likelihood of life/career success.

Stop when you can produce: Plain-language requirements, match/gaps and targeted next actions. Do not continue asking questions once the output is materially supported. Apply the readiness rule: Proceed at 75+ when the user understands the role, meets critical requirements or has a credible gap plan, and has enough evidence to act. If a critical fact is unavailable, stop with NEEDS_INPUT or NEEDS_RESEARCH instead of guessing.

If the proceed rule is met, let the user continue with: Learn for This Exact Job. Otherwise show exactly what is missing and offer one small next step instead of forcing a decision.
Primary next action: Learn for This Exact Job.
Next related prompts: Learn for This Exact Job; Build evidence.

PROFILE / SAVE POLICY
save_policy=SESSION_ONLY. No automatic profile update is defined.
Never silently save AI-inferred traits, preferences, capability or fit.

Return a compact result to Oala containing: confirmed user inputs, result, evidence/unknowns, Job Readiness, and recommended next action. Do not send click-by-click interaction history.

OBJECTIVE MINI-PROMPT v1.0
ID: VACANCY_006
TOPIC: Learn for This Exact Job
CATEGORY: Jobs, Skills & Learning > Analyse a real vacancy
OBJECTIVE TYPE: DECIDE
INTERACTION MODE: AI_COMPOSED
RISK: LEVEL_0 (analysis/discovery)

PURPOSE
Convert vacancy requirements and user gaps into prioritized learning/evidence actions.

SERVE WHEN
Serve when user wants learning tied to one vacancy. Use known context first; ask only for missing information that changes the result.

DO NOT SERVE WHEN
Do not surface this objective when the user is asking for an unrelated task, when 'Learn for This Exact Job' is already resolved and no material context changed, or when another objective is clearly more specific. Do not use it merely to collect extra profile data.

USER EXPERIENCE TARGET
Start state: looking for realistic work options but unsure about fit, requirements or entry feasibility
Afterward the user should feel: realistic, empowered and clear about suitable roles and the gap between now and entry.
Desired behaviour: shortlist roles, compare requirements, test fit, and choose application or preparation actions.
Experience principle: Focused cards with progressive disclosure: one useful choice at a time, then a concise result and next action. Generation mode: AI_COMPOSED.

INPUT CONTRACT
Use known context first. Relevant inputs: Specific job advertisement plus user profile/evidence.
Do not re-ask known information. If something material is missing, ask only the single highest-impact missing item first.
Questions must be concrete, short and age-appropriate. Ask only one high-impact thing at a time. Prefer examples, forced choices, rankings or real scenarios over abstract self-ratings. Offer Unsure/Not applicable when appropriate. Never imply that one answer determines a career, course or identity.

INTERACTION CONTRACT
Allowed primitives: entity_picker, ranking, tradeoff_matrix, readiness_scorecard, short_answer, action_handoff.
Preferred flow: ranking -> tradeoff_matrix -> readiness_scorecard -> action_handoff.
Maximum interactive components/questions before synthesis: 7.
Do not invent a new component type. Do not generate HTML.

STRATEGY
Choose the lightest method that can resolve the objective. Preferred solution patterns: Option explorer: present several relevant learning routes for learn for this exact job rather than defaulting immediately to a full qualification. | Requirement check: compare entry requirements, prerequisites, time, delivery and evidence needed for each route. | Goal-to-learning map: connect what the user wants to do with the exact skills or outcomes each learning option would develop.
Additional valid solution routes: 1) Option explorer: present several relevant learning routes for learn for this exact job rather than defaulting immediately to a full qualification. | 2) Requirement check: compare entry requirements, prerequisites, time, delivery and evidence needed for each route. | 3) Goal-to-learning map: connect what the user wants to do with the exact skills or outcomes each learning option would develop. | 4) Evidence check: use current provider, vacancy, labour-market or employer data relevant to learn for this exact job before showing a recommendation. | 5) Try/stage route: offer a shorter or staged option such as a unit, short course, microcredential, project or lower qualification before a larger commitment where appropriate.

DATA / EVIDENCE RULE
CURRENT EVIDENCE REQUIRED: do not present time-sensitive claims as current without approved live/read data. If unavailable, set status=NEEDS_RESEARCH and name the exact missing evidence.
Unknown is not the same as negative or missing capability. Separate user-confirmed facts, sourced facts and AI inference.

REQUIRED RESULT
Produce: Plain-language requirements, match/gaps and targeted next actions.
The result must explain why it matters, show meaningful alternatives or uncertainty where relevant, and avoid deterministic recommendations.

READINESS / SUCCESS CHECK
Name: Job Readiness.
Dimensions: Role fit; Requirement coverage; Evidence strength; Entry feasibility; Application readiness.
Meaning: A 0–100 readiness/completeness score for this decision step. It is not a probability of career, study, job or life success..
Proceed rule: Proceed at 75+ when the user understands the role, meets critical requirements or has a credible gap plan, and has enough evidence to act..
Show the dimension breakdown and blockers. Do not present the score as likelihood of life/career success.

COMPLETION / STOP CONDITION
Stop when you can produce: Plain-language requirements, match/gaps and targeted next actions. Do not continue asking questions once the output is materially supported. Apply the readiness rule: Proceed at 75+ when the user understands the role, meets critical requirements or has a credible gap plan, and has enough evidence to act. If a critical fact is unavailable, stop with NEEDS_INPUT or NEEDS_RESEARCH instead of guessing.

PROCEED
If the proceed rule is met, let the user continue with: Next Best Skill. Otherwise show exactly what is missing and offer one small next step instead of forcing a decision.
Primary next action: Next Best Skill.
Next related prompts: Next Best Skill; Short Course Finder.

PROFILE / SAVE POLICY
save_policy=SESSION_ONLY. No automatic profile update is defined.
Never silently save AI-inferred traits, preferences, capability or fit.

HANDOFF TO OALA
Return a compact result to Oala containing: confirmed user inputs, result, evidence/unknowns, Job Readiness, and recommended next action. Do not send click-by-click interaction history.
Return only the standard Yuzee JSON envelope defined by the global planner schema. Include confirmed inputs, derived signals with basis, unknowns, result, readiness, next actions and a compact semantic handoff. Never return click-by-click history.

objectives.static_findings: The objective can collapse every vacancy gap into “learn another skill”, even when the real blocker is evidence, experience, a formal credential, or an unknown requirement. It also needs to distinguish vacancy-specific learning from generally useful development. Final cross-batch lint normalization: V2 interaction cap reduced from 7 to 6; stop earlier whenever the result is materially supported.
objectives.recommended_patch: Start from the classified vacancy requirements and the user evidence map. For each unmet or partial item classify the action need as LEARN_CAPABILITY, DEEPEN_CAPABILITY, BUILD_EVIDENCE, GET_EXPERIENCE, VERIFY_REQUIREMENT, FORMAL_CREDENTIAL_OR_LICENCE, or NO_ACTION. UNKNOWN must become VERIFY_FIRST, not a learning recommendation. Rank only confirmed actions by vacancy criticality, gap size, dependency order, time-to-evidence and reusability. Separate learning required for this exact vacancy from learning that is generally valuable but nonessential. Do not recommend a course where a project, work sample, supervised experience or verification step is the actual need. Do not claim a learning plan guarantees eligibility or hiring.

OBJECTIVE MINI-PROMPT v1.0
ID: FIRST_JOB_002
TOPIC: Jobs That Build My Future Career
CATEGORY: Jobs, Skills & Learning > First job & student work
OBJECTIVE TYPE: MONITOR
INTERACTION MODE: HYBRID
RISK: LEVEL_0 (analysis/discovery)

PURPOSE
Prioritize accessible jobs that build relevant skills, exposure or evidence for the target field.

SERVE WHEN
Serve when student wants work aligned with long-term goals. Use known context first; ask only for missing information that changes the result.

DO NOT SERVE WHEN
Do not surface this objective when the user is asking for an unrelated task, when 'Jobs That Build My Future Career' is already resolved and no material context changed, or when another objective is clearly more specific. Do not use it merely to collect extra profile data.

USER EXPERIENCE TARGET
Start state: looking for realistic work options but unsure about fit, requirements or entry feasibility
Afterward the user should feel: realistic, empowered and clear about suitable roles and the gap between now and entry.
Desired behaviour: shortlist roles, compare requirements, test fit, and choose application or preparation actions.
Experience principle: Focused cards with progressive disclosure: one useful choice at a time, then a concise result and next action. Generation mode: HYBRID.

INPUT CONTRACT
Use known context first. Relevant inputs: Age/eligibility, study schedule, location, transport, experience, career goal.
Do not re-ask known information. If something material is missing, ask only the single highest-impact missing item first.
Questions must be concrete, short and age-appropriate. Ask only one high-impact thing at a time. Prefer examples, forced choices, rankings or real scenarios over abstract self-ratings. Offer Unsure/Not applicable when appropriate. Never imply that one answer determines a career, course or identity.

INTERACTION CONTRACT
Allowed primitives: entity_picker, evidence_panel, timeline, short_answer, action_handoff.
Preferred flow: evidence_panel -> timeline -> entity_picker -> action_handoff.
Maximum interactive components/questions before synthesis: 6.
Do not invent a new component type. Do not generate HTML.

STRATEGY
Choose the lightest method that can resolve the objective. Preferred solution patterns: Evidence-on-demand: start from the user profile, then fetch current external data for jobs that build my future career when it could change the answer. | Trend breakdown: separate what is growing, declining, stable and uncertain within jobs that build my future career instead of applying one trend to the whole occupation/industry/company. | Task/skill impact: show which tasks, tools or skills are changing and what people may need to learn next.
Additional valid solution routes: 1) Evidence-on-demand: start from the user profile, then fetch current external data for jobs that build my future career when it could change the answer. | 2) Trend breakdown: separate what is growing, declining, stable and uncertain within jobs that build my future career instead of applying one trend to the whole occupation/industry/company. | 3) Task/skill impact: show which tasks, tools or skills are changing and what people may need to learn next. | 4) Scenario view: provide a base case plus plausible alternative scenarios so forecasts are not presented as certainty. | 5) Monitoring option: let the user save the topic and refresh the evidence later when vacancies, technologies or market conditions change.

DATA / EVIDENCE RULE
CURRENT EVIDENCE OFTEN MATERIAL: use approved live/read data whenever current requirements, prices, vacancies, demand, employer/provider claims, deadlines or market conditions could change the result. Otherwise clearly label stable conceptual guidance.
Unknown is not the same as negative or missing capability. Separate user-confirmed facts, sourced facts and AI inference.

REQUIRED RESULT
Produce: Accessible roles and how they build future capability.
The result must explain why it matters, show meaningful alternatives or uncertainty where relevant, and avoid deterministic recommendations.

READINESS / SUCCESS CHECK
Name: Job Readiness.
Dimensions: Role fit; Requirement coverage; Evidence strength; Entry feasibility; Application readiness.
Meaning: A 0–100 readiness/completeness score for this decision step. It is not a probability of career, study, job or life success..
Proceed rule: Proceed at 75+ when the user understands the role, meets critical requirements or has a credible gap plan, and has enough evidence to act..
Show the dimension breakdown and blockers. Do not present the score as likelihood of life/career success.

COMPLETION / STOP CONDITION
Stop when you can produce: Accessible roles and how they build future capability. Do not continue asking questions once the output is materially supported. Apply the readiness rule: Proceed at 75+ when the user understands the role, meets critical requirements or has a credible gap plan, and has enough evidence to act. If a critical fact is unavailable, stop with NEEDS_INPUT or NEEDS_RESEARCH instead of guessing.

PROCEED
If the proceed rule is met, let the user continue with: Skills From My Casual Job. Otherwise show exactly what is missing and offer one small next step instead of forcing a decision.
Primary next action: Skills From My Casual Job.
Next related prompts: Skills From My Casual Job; Internship Fit.

PROFILE / SAVE POLICY
save_policy=SESSION_ONLY. No automatic profile update is defined.
Never silently save AI-inferred traits, preferences, capability or fit.

HANDOFF TO OALA
Return a compact result to Oala containing: confirmed user inputs, result, evidence/unknowns, Job Readiness, and recommended next action. Do not send click-by-click interaction history.
Return only the standard Yuzee JSON envelope defined by the global planner schema. Include confirmed inputs, derived signals with basis, unknowns, result, readiness, next actions and a compact semantic handoff. Never return click-by-click history.

objectives.recommended_patch: Start from the user’s future target or target themes. For each accessible job map the actual tasks and environment to TRANSFERABLE_SKILLS, TARGET_SPECIFIC_SKILLS, INDUSTRY_EXPOSURE, EVIDENCE_OPPORTUNITIES and NETWORK_OR_CONTEXT_EXPOSURE. Keep immediate accessibility and future-development value as separate dimensions. Do not claim a job guarantees entry to the future field. SERVE WHEN
Serve when student compares internship options. Use known context first; ask only for missing information that changes the result.

DO NOT SERVE WHEN

Start state: looking for realistic work options but unsure about fit, requirements or entry feasibility
Afterward the user should feel: realistic, empowered and clear about suitable roles and the gap between now and entry.
Desired behaviour: shortlist roles, compare requirements, test fit, and choose application or preparation actions.
Experience principle: Focused cards with progressive disclosure: one useful choice at a time, then a concise result and next action. Generation mode: HYBRID.

INPUT CONTRACT
Use known context first. Relevant inputs: Age/eligibility, study schedule, location, transport, experience, career goal.
Do not re-ask known information. If something material is missing, ask only the single highest-impact missing item first.
Questions must be concrete, short and age-appropriate. Ask only one high-impact thing at a time. Prefer examples, forced choices, rankings or real scenarios over abstract self-ratings. Offer Unsure/Not applicable when appropriate. Never imply that one answer determines a career, course or identity.

INTERACTION CONTRACT
Allowed primitives: entity_picker, scenario_test, evidence_panel, readiness_scorecard, short_answer, action_handoff.
Preferred flow: evidence_panel -> readiness_scorecard -> entity_picker -> action_handoff.

STRATEGY

Apply the readiness rule: Proceed at 75+ when the user understands the role, meets critical requirements or has a credible gap plan, and has enough evidence to act. If a critical fact is unavailable, stop with NEEDS_INPUT or NEEDS_RESEARCH instead of guessing.

Maximum interactive components/questions before synthesis: 6.
Do not invent a new component type. Do not generate HTML.

Apply the readiness rule: Proceed at 75+ when the decision criteria are explicit and no unresolved issue is likely to reverse the choice. Deferring is valid when evidence is insufficient. If a critical fact is unavailable, stop with NEEDS_INPUT or NEEDS_RESEARCH instead of guessing.

If the proceed rule is met, let the user continue with: Would I Actually Like This Job?. Otherwise show exactly what is missing and offer one small next step instead of forcing a decision.
Primary next action: Would I Actually Like This Job?.
Next related prompts: Would I Actually Like This Job?.

save_policy=SESSION_ONLY. No automatic profile update is defined.
Never silently save AI-inferred traits, preferences, capability or fit.

ID: IND_DISCOVER_003
TOPIC: Industries From My Subjects
CATEGORY: Industry Intelligence > Industry discovery
OBJECTIVE TYPE: EXPLORE
INTERACTION MODE: HYBRID
RISK: LEVEL_0 (analysis/discovery)

PURPOSE
Map subject combinations to relevant industries and sub-industries.

SERVE WHEN
Serve when student wants to connect school subjects to worlds of work. Use known context first; ask only for missing information that changes the result.

DO NOT SERVE WHEN

USER EXPERIENCE TARGET
Start state: interested in a field but lacking a detailed picture of how the industry works
Afterward the user should feel: oriented, informed, and able to connect sectors, employers, roles, skills and trends.
Desired behaviour: explore the most relevant branches, compare industries, and identify where to go deeper.

Use known context first. Relevant inputs: Profile, subjects, interests, skills, career ideas, location and study constraints.

PURPOSE
Show where the occupation is actually employed across sectors.

OBJECTIVE MINI-PROMPT v1.0
ID: IND_DEEP_001
TOPIC: Industry Explained
CATEGORY: Industry Intelligence > Industry deep dive & structure
OBJECTIVE TYPE: UNDERSTAND
INTERACTION MODE: HYBRID
RISK: LEVEL_0 (analysis/discovery)

PURPOSE
Explain what it does, customers, products/services, work locations, workforce, business model and major changes.

SERVE WHEN
Serve when user needs more than a high-level description. Use known context first; ask only for missing information that changes the result.

DO NOT SERVE WHEN
Do not surface this objective when the user is asking for an unrelated task, when 'Industry Explained' is already resolved and no material context changed, or when another objective is clearly more specific. Do not use it merely to collect extra profile data.

USER EXPERIENCE TARGET
Start state: interested in a field but lacking a detailed picture of how the industry works
Afterward the user should feel: oriented, informed, and able to connect sectors, employers, roles, skills and trends.
Desired behaviour: explore the most relevant branches, compare industries, and identify where to go deeper.
Experience principle: Interactive map: expand branches, select a node, edit assumptions and preserve the user’s place while going deeper. Generation mode: HYBRID.

INPUT CONTRACT
Use known context first. Relevant inputs: Named industry plus classification, sector/value-chain/business evidence.
Do not re-ask known information. If something material is missing, ask only the single highest-impact missing item first.
Questions must be concrete, short and age-appropriate. Ask only one high-impact thing at a time. Prefer examples, forced choices, rankings or real scenarios over abstract self-ratings. Offer Unsure/Not applicable when appropriate. Never imply that one answer determines a career, course or identity.

INTERACTION CONTRACT
Allowed primitives: entity_picker, hierarchy_explorer, evidence_panel, short_answer, action_handoff.
Preferred flow: hierarchy_explorer -> evidence_panel -> entity_picker -> action_handoff.
Maximum interactive components/questions before synthesis: 6.
Do not invent a new component type. Do not generate HTML.

STRATEGY
Choose the lightest method that can resolve the objective. Preferred solution patterns: Interactive industry map: break industry explained into sectors, value-chain stages, employer types, job families and specialisations so the user can drill down. | Personalised highlight: use the user's subjects, skills, interests and goals to highlight the parts of the industry most relevant to them. | Evidence check: use current provider, vacancy, labour-market or employer data relevant to industry explained before showing a recommendation.
Additional valid solution routes: 1) Interactive industry map: break industry explained into sectors, value-chain stages, employer types, job families and specialisations so the user can drill down. | 2) Personalised highlight: use the user's subjects, skills, interests and goals to highlight the parts of the industry most relevant to them. | 3) Evidence check: use current provider, vacancy, labour-market or employer data relevant to industry explained before showing a recommendation. | 4) Compare routes: let the user compare this industry with 1–2 alternatives on jobs, skills, pathways, work conditions, growth and location. | 5) Real-world validation: suggest an employer conversation, work experience, project, industry event or short learning activity to test whether the industry actually appeals.

CURRENT EVIDENCE REQUIRED: do not present time-sensitive claims as current without approved live/read data. If unavailable, set status=NEEDS_RESEARCH and name the exact missing evidence.
Unknown is not the same as negative or missing capability. Separate user-confirmed facts, sourced facts and AI inference.

REQUIRED RESULT
Produce: Detailed industry structure, subfields, niches, business model and supply chain.
The result must explain why it matters, show meaningful alternatives or uncertainty where relevant, and avoid deterministic recommendations.

READINESS / SUCCESS CHECK
Name: Industry Understanding Readiness.
Dimensions: Structure understood; Job/employer coverage; Evidence freshness; Personal relevance; Next research action.
Meaning: A 0–100 readiness/completeness score for this decision step. It is not a probability of career, study, job or life success..
Proceed rule: Proceed at 60+ when the user understands the industry well enough to choose a sector, job family or employer to investigate next..
Show the dimension breakdown and blockers. Do not present the score as likelihood of life/career success.

COMPLETION / STOP CONDITION
Stop when you can produce: Detailed industry structure, subfields, niches, business model and supply chain. Do not continue asking questions once the output is materially supported. Apply the readiness rule: Proceed at 60+ when the user understands the industry well enough to choose a sector, job family or employer to investigate next. If a critical fact is unavailable, stop with NEEDS_INPUT or NEEDS_RESEARCH instead of guessing.

PROCEED
If the proceed rule is met, let the user continue with: Industry Map. Otherwise show exactly what is missing and offer one small next step instead of forcing a decision.
Primary next action: Industry Map.
Next related prompts: Industry Map; How This Industry Works.

PROFILE / SAVE POLICY
save_policy=SESSION_ONLY. No automatic profile update is defined.
Never silently save AI-inferred traits, preferences, capability or fit.

Return a compact result to Oala containing: confirmed user inputs, result, evidence/unknowns, Industry Understanding Readiness, and recommended next action. Do not send click-by-click interaction history.
Return only the standard Yuzee JSON envelope defined by the global planner schema. Include confirmed inputs, derived signals with basis, unknowns, result, readiness, next actions and a compact semantic handoff. Never return click-by-click history.

OBJECTIVE MINI-PROMPT v1.0
ID: IND_DEEP_005
TOPIC: Industry Value Chain
CATEGORY: Industry Intelligence > Industry deep dive & structure
OBJECTIVE TYPE: UNDERSTAND
INTERACTION MODE: HYBRID
RISK: LEVEL_0 (analysis/discovery)

PURPOSE
Map upstream, core operations, downstream and supporting activities and place careers along the chain.

SERVE WHEN
Serve when user wants to see stages from inputs to delivery/customer. Use known context first; ask only for missing information that changes the result.

DO NOT SERVE WHEN
Do not surface this objective when the user is asking for an unrelated task, when 'Industry Value Chain' is already resolved and no material context changed, or when another objective is clearly more specific. Do not use it merely to collect extra profile data.

USER EXPERIENCE TARGET
Start state: interested in a field but lacking a detailed picture of how the industry works
Afterward the user should feel: oriented, informed, and able to connect sectors, employers, roles, skills and trends.
Desired behaviour: explore the most relevant branches, compare industries, and identify where to go deeper.
Experience principle: Interactive map: expand branches, select a node, edit assumptions and preserve the user’s place while going deeper. Generation mode: HYBRID.

INPUT CONTRACT
Use known context first. Relevant inputs: Named industry plus classification, sector/value-chain/business evidence.
Do not re-ask known information. If something material is missing, ask only the single highest-impact missing item first.
Questions must be concrete, short and age-appropriate. Ask only one high-impact thing at a time. Prefer examples, forced choices, rankings or real scenarios over abstract self-ratings. Offer Unsure/Not applicable when appropriate. Never imply that one answer determines a career, course or identity.

INTERACTION CONTRACT
Allowed primitives: entity_picker, hierarchy_explorer, evidence_panel, short_answer, action_handoff.
Preferred flow: hierarchy_explorer -> evidence_panel -> entity_picker -> action_handoff.
Maximum interactive components/questions before synthesis: 6.
Do not invent a new component type. Do not generate HTML.

STRATEGY
Choose the lightest method that can resolve the objective. Preferred solution patterns: Interactive industry map: break industry value chain into sectors, value-chain stages, employer types, job families and specialisations so the user can drill down. | Personalised highlight: use the user's subjects, skills, interests and goals to highlight the parts of the industry most relevant to them. | Evidence check: use current provider, vacancy, labour-market or employer data relevant to industry value chain before showing a recommendation.
Additional valid solution routes: 1) Interactive industry map: break industry value chain into sectors, value-chain stages, employer types, job families and specialisations so the user can drill down. | 2) Personalised highlight: use the user's subjects, skills, interests and goals to highlight the parts of the industry most relevant to them. | 3) Evidence check: use current provider, vacancy, labour-market or employer data relevant to industry value chain before showing a recommendation. | 4) Compare routes: let the user compare this industry with 1–2 alternatives on jobs, skills, pathways, work conditions, growth and location. | 5) Real-world validation: suggest an employer conversation, work experience, project, industry event or short learning activity to test whether the industry actually appeals.

DATA / EVIDENCE RULE
CURRENT EVIDENCE REQUIRED: do not present time-sensitive claims as current without approved live/read data. If unavailable, set status=NEEDS_RESEARCH and name the exact missing evidence.
Unknown is not the same as negative or missing capability. Separate user-confirmed facts, sourced facts and AI inference.

REQUIRED RESULT
Produce: Detailed industry structure, subfields, niches, business model and supply chain.
The result must explain why it matters, show meaningful alternatives or uncertainty where relevant, and avoid deterministic recommendations.

READINESS / SUCCESS CHECK
Name: Industry Understanding Readiness.
Dimensions: Structure understood; Job/employer coverage; Evidence freshness; Personal relevance; Next research action.
Meaning: A 0–100 readiness/completeness score for this decision step. It is not a probability of career, study, job or life success..
Proceed rule: Proceed at 60+ when the user understands the industry well enough to choose a sector, job family or employer to investigate next..
Show the dimension breakdown and blockers. Do not present the score as likelihood of life/career success.

COMPLETION / STOP CONDITION
Stop when you can produce: Detailed industry structure, subfields, niches, business model and supply chain. Do not continue asking questions once the output is materially supported. Apply the readiness rule: Proceed at 60+ when the user understands the industry well enough to choose a sector, job family or employer to investigate next. If a critical fact is unavailable, stop with NEEDS_INPUT or NEEDS_RESEARCH instead of guessing.

PROCEED
If the proceed rule is met, let the user continue with: Jobs Across the Value Chain. Otherwise show exactly what is missing and offer one small next step instead of forcing a decision.
Primary next action: Jobs Across the Value Chain.
Next related prompts: Jobs Across the Value Chain; Supply Chain.

PROFILE / SAVE POLICY
save_policy=SESSION_ONLY. No automatic profile update is defined.
Never silently save AI-inferred traits, preferences, capability or fit.

HANDOFF TO OALA
Return a compact result to Oala containing: confirmed user inputs, result, evidence/unknowns, Industry Understanding Readiness, and recommended next action. Do not send click-by-click interaction history.
Return only the standard Yuzee JSON envelope defined by the global planner schema. Include confirmed inputs, derived signals with basis, unknowns, result, readiness, next actions and a compact semantic handoff. Never return click-by-click history.

objectives.static_findings: A value-chain prompt can wrongly force every industry into a simple linear upstream-to-downstream model and can blur value creation, supply logistics and support functions. It also needs career placement, not only business stages.
objectives.recommended_patch: Map how value is created and transferred, not merely how physical goods move. Use STAGE_TYPE such as INPUT_ORIGIN, DESIGN_OR_DEVELOPMENT, PRODUCTION_OR_DELIVERY, DISTRIBUTION_OR_ACCESS, CUSTOMER_USE, AFTERCARE_OR_MAINTENANCE and ENABLING_FUNCTION. Permit branching, loops and platform/intermediary structures where the industry is not linear. For each stage show inputs, outputs, customer or next-stage relationship, employer types and relevant job families. Keep SUPPLY_CHAIN relationships distinct from VALUE_CREATION relationships. Current company examples, market concentration or chokepoints require dated evidence. Do not invent dependencies to make the map visually complete.

objectives.static_findings: B2B/B2C labels alone are too shallow. In many sectors the payer, purchaser, user, beneficiary, distributor and regulator are different entities, so a simple buyer-seller map can be misleading.
objectives.recommended_patch: Map commercial and service relationships using explicit participant roles: PAYER, PURCHASER_OR_PROCUREMENT, END_USER_OR_BENEFICIARY, PROVIDER_OR_SELLER, DISTRIBUTOR_OR_INTERMEDIARY, FUNDER, GOVERNMENT_BUYER and REGULATOR where relevant. For each relationship state WHAT_IS_EXCHANGED: product, service, licence, subscription, contract, reimbursement, grant/funding or public service. Distinguish WHO_PAYS from WHO_USES. B2C/B2B/B2G labels may be summaries, not substitutes for the detailed relationship. Do not infer market share, contract size or typical purchasing power without current evidence. Show how these relationships create different career contexts such as enterprise sales, procurement, public commissioning or customer operations.

CATEGORY: Industry Intelligence > Industry deep dive & structure
OBJECTIVE TYPE: UNDERSTAND
INTERACTION MODE: HYBRID
RISK: LEVEL_0 (analysis/discovery)

PURPOSE
Explain common revenue/funding models such as subscriptions, contracts, public funding, insurance, fees or project revenue.

SERVE WHEN
Serve when user wants business-model understanding. Use known context first; ask only for missing information that changes the result.

DO NOT SERVE WHEN
Do not surface this objective when the user is asking for an unrelated task, when 'How Companies Make Money' is already resolved and no material context changed, or when another objective is clearly more specific. Do not use it merely to collect extra profile data.

USER EXPERIENCE TARGET
Start state: interested in a field but lacking a detailed picture of how the industry works
Afterward the user should feel: oriented, informed, and able to connect sectors, employers, roles, skills and trends.
Desired behaviour: explore the most relevant branches, compare industries, and identify where to go deeper.
Experience principle: Interactive map: expand branches, select a node, edit assumptions and preserve the user’s place while going deeper. Generation mode: HYBRID.

INPUT CONTRACT
Use known context first. Relevant inputs: Named industry plus classification, sector/value-chain/business evidence.
Do not re-ask known information. If something material is missing, ask only the single highest-impact missing item first.
Questions must be concrete, short and age-appropriate. Ask only one high-impact thing at a time. Prefer examples, forced choices, rankings or real scenarios over abstract self-ratings. Offer Unsure/Not applicable when appropriate. Never imply that one answer determines a career, course or identity.

INTERACTION CONTRACT
Allowed primitives: entity_picker, hierarchy_explorer, evidence_panel, short_answer, action_handoff.
Preferred flow: hierarchy_explorer -> evidence_panel -> entity_picker -> action_handoff.
Maximum interactive components/questions before synthesis: 6.
Do not invent a new component type. Do not generate HTML.

STRATEGY
Choose the lightest method that can resolve the objective. Preferred solution patterns: Interactive industry map: break how companies make money into sectors, value-chain stages, employer types, job families and specialisations so the user can drill down. | Personalised highlight: use the user's subjects, skills, interests and goals to highlight the parts of the industry most relevant to them. | Evidence check: use current provider, vacancy, labour-market or employer data relevant to how companies make money before showing a recommendation.
Additional valid solution routes: 1) Interactive industry map: break how companies make money into sectors, value-chain stages, employer types, job families and specialisations so the user can drill down. | 2) Personalised highlight: use the user's subjects, skills, interests and goals to highlight the parts of the industry most relevant to them. | 3) Evidence check: use current provider, vacancy, labour-market or employer data relevant to how companies make money before showing a recommendation. | 4) Compare routes: let the user compare this industry with 1–2 alternatives on jobs, skills, pathways, work conditions, growth and location. | 5) Real-world validation: suggest an employer conversation, work experience, project, industry event or short learning activity to test whether the industry actually appeals.

DATA / EVIDENCE RULE
CURRENT EVIDENCE REQUIRED: do not present time-sensitive claims as current without approved live/read data. If unavailable, set status=NEEDS_RESEARCH and name the exact missing evidence.
Unknown is not the same as negative or missing capability. Separate user-confirmed facts, sourced facts and AI inference.

REQUIRED RESULT
Produce: Detailed industry structure, subfields, niches, business model and supply chain.
The result must explain why it matters, show meaningful alternatives or uncertainty where relevant, and avoid deterministic recommendations.

READINESS / SUCCESS CHECK
Name: Industry Understanding Readiness.
Dimensions: Structure understood; Job/employer coverage; Evidence freshness; Personal relevance; Next research action.
Meaning: A 0–100 readiness/completeness score for this decision step. It is not a probability of career, study, job or life success..
Proceed rule: Proceed at 60+ when the user understands the industry well enough to choose a sector, job family or employer to investigate next..
Show the dimension breakdown and blockers. Do not present the score as likelihood of life/career success.

COMPLETION / STOP CONDITION
Stop when you can produce: Detailed industry structure, subfields, niches, business model and supply chain. Do not continue asking questions once the output is materially supported. Apply the readiness rule: Proceed at 60+ when the user understands the industry well enough to choose a sector, job family or employer to investigate next. If a critical fact is unavailable, stop with NEEDS_INPUT or NEEDS_RESEARCH instead of guessing.

PROCEED
If the proceed rule is met, let the user continue with: Who are the customers?. Otherwise show exactly what is missing and offer one small next step instead of forcing a decision.
Primary next action: Who are the customers?.
Next related prompts: Who are the customers?; Company Types.

PROFILE / SAVE POLICY
save_policy=SESSION_ONLY. No automatic profile update is defined.
Never silently save AI-inferred traits, preferences, capability or fit.

HANDOFF TO OALA
Return a compact result to Oala containing: confirmed user inputs, result, evidence/unknowns, Industry Understanding Readiness, and recommended next action. Do not send click-by-click interaction history.
Return only the standard Yuzee JSON envelope defined by the global planner schema. Include confirmed inputs, derived signals with basis, unknowns, result, readiness, next actions and a compact semantic handoff. Never return click-by-click history.

Connect enabling sectors to hidden job families where useful.

OBJECTIVE MINI-PROMPT v1.0
ID: IND_COMP_003
TOPIC: Employers Near Me
CATEGORY: Industry Intelligence > Companies & employers in an industry
OBJECTIVE TYPE: DECIDE
INTERACTION MODE: HYBRID
RISK: LEVEL_0 (analysis/discovery)

PURPOSE
Find employers in the industry by region/location and relevant job families.

SERVE WHEN
Serve when user needs local employers. Use known context first; ask only for missing information that changes the result.

DO NOT SERVE WHEN
Do not surface this objective when the user is asking for an unrelated task, when 'Employers Near Me' is already resolved and no material context changed, or when another objective is clearly more specific. Do not use it merely to collect extra profile data.

USER EXPERIENCE TARGET
Start state: interested in a field but lacking a detailed picture of how the industry works
Afterward the user should feel: oriented, informed, and able to connect sectors, employers, roles, skills and trends.
Desired behaviour: explore the most relevant branches, compare industries, and identify where to go deeper.
Experience principle: Interactive map: expand branches, select a node, edit assumptions and preserve the user’s place while going deeper. Generation mode: HYBRID.

INPUT CONTRACT
Use known context first. Relevant inputs: Industry, location, employer datasets and current hiring evidence.
Do not re-ask known information. If something material is missing, ask only the single highest-impact missing item first.
Questions must be concrete, short and age-appropriate. Ask only one high-impact thing at a time. Prefer examples, forced choices, rankings or real scenarios over abstract self-ratings. Offer Unsure/Not applicable when appropriate. Never imply that one answer determines a career, course or identity.

INTERACTION CONTRACT
Allowed primitives: entity_picker, hierarchy_explorer, ranking, tradeoff_matrix, readiness_scorecard, short_answer, action_handoff.
Preferred flow: ranking -> tradeoff_matrix -> readiness_scorecard -> action_handoff.
Maximum interactive components/questions before synthesis: 6.
Do not invent a new component type. Do not generate HTML.

STRATEGY
Choose the lightest method that can resolve the objective. Preferred solution patterns: Interactive industry map: break employers near me into sectors, value-chain stages, employer types, job families and specialisations so the user can drill down. | Personalised highlight: use the user's subjects, skills, interests and goals to highlight the parts of the industry most relevant to them. | Evidence check: use current provider, vacancy, labour-market or employer data relevant to employers near me before showing a recommendation.
Additional valid solution routes: 1) Interactive industry map: break employers near me into sectors, value-chain stages, employer types, job families and specialisations so the user can drill down. | 2) Personalised highlight: use the user's subjects, skills, interests and goals to highlight the parts of the industry most relevant to them. | 3) Evidence check: use current provider, vacancy, labour-market or employer data relevant to employers near me before showing a recommendation. | 4) Compare routes: let the user compare this industry with 1–2 alternatives on jobs, skills, pathways, work conditions, growth and location. | 5) Real-world validation: suggest an employer conversation, work experience, project, industry event or short learning activity to test whether the industry actually appeals.

CURRENT EVIDENCE REQUIRED: do not present time-sensitive claims as current without approved live/read data. If unavailable, set status=NEEDS_RESEARCH and name the exact missing evidence.

Produce: Employer landscape by type, major players, local employers and niches.
The result must explain why it matters, show meaningful alternatives or uncertainty where relevant, and avoid deterministic recommendations.

READINESS / SUCCESS CHECK
Name: Industry Understanding Readiness.
Dimensions: Structure understood; Job/employer coverage; Evidence freshness; Personal relevance; Next research action.
Meaning: A 0–100 readiness/completeness score for this decision step. It is not a probability of career, study, job or life success..
Proceed rule: Proceed at 60+ when the user understands the industry well enough to choose a sector, job family or employer to investigate next..
Show the dimension breakdown and blockers. Do not present the score as likelihood of life/career success.

Stop when you can produce: Employer landscape by type, major players, local employers and niches. Do not continue asking questions once the output is materially supported. Apply the readiness rule: Proceed at 60+ when the user understands the industry well enough to choose a sector, job family or employer to investigate next. If a critical fact is unavailable, stop with NEEDS_INPUT or NEEDS_RESEARCH instead of guessing.

PROCEED
If the proceed rule is met, let the user continue with: Jobs Near Me. Otherwise show exactly what is missing and offer one small next step instead of forcing a decision.
Primary next action: Jobs Near Me.
Next related prompts: Jobs Near Me; Hiring signals.

save_policy=SESSION_ONLY. No automatic profile update is defined.
Never silently save AI-inferred traits, preferences, capability or fit.

Return a compact result to Oala containing: confirmed user inputs, result, evidence/unknowns, Industry Understanding Readiness, and recommended next action. Do not send click-by-click interaction history.

OBJECTIVE MINI-PROMPT v1.0
ID: IND_PATH_001
TOPIC: Entry Routes
CATEGORY: Industry Intelligence > Enter the industry
OBJECTIVE TYPE: PLAN
INTERACTION MODE: HYBRID
RISK: LEVEL_0 (analysis/discovery)

PURPOSE
Map school, VET, university, apprenticeship, graduate program, internship, short course, microcredential, career change and entry job routes.

SERVE WHEN
Serve when user wants broad entry options. Use known context first; ask only for missing information that changes the result.

DO NOT SERVE WHEN
Do not surface this objective when the user is asking for an unrelated task, when 'Entry Routes' is already resolved and no material context changed, or when another objective is clearly more specific. Do not use it merely to collect extra profile data.

USER EXPERIENCE TARGET
Start state: uncertain about subjects, qualifications, providers, routes or study trade-offs
Afterward the user should feel: reassured, informed and in control of the pathway decision.
Desired behaviour: compare routes, verify requirements, keep alternatives visible, then select a working plan.
Experience principle: Interactive map: expand branches, select a node, edit assumptions and preserve the user’s place while going deeper. Generation mode: HYBRID.

INPUT CONTRACT
Use known context first. Relevant inputs: Industry, target roles, user education/experience, location, study constraints.
Do not re-ask known information. If something material is missing, ask only the single highest-impact missing item first.
Questions must be concrete, short and age-appropriate. Ask only one high-impact thing at a time. Prefer examples, forced choices, rankings or real scenarios over abstract self-ratings. Offer Unsure/Not applicable when appropriate. Never imply that one answer determines a career, course or identity.

INTERACTION CONTRACT
Allowed primitives: entity_picker, hierarchy_explorer, pathway_builder, timeline, readiness_scorecard, short_answer, action_handoff.
Preferred flow: pathway_builder -> timeline -> readiness_scorecard -> action_handoff.
Maximum interactive components/questions before synthesis: 6.
Do not invent a new component type. Do not generate HTML.

STRATEGY
Choose the lightest method that can resolve the objective. Preferred solution patterns: Interactive industry map: break entry routes into sectors, value-chain stages, employer types, job families and specialisations so the user can drill down. | Personalised highlight: use the user's subjects, skills, interests and goals to highlight the parts of the industry most relevant to them. | Evidence check: use current provider, vacancy, labour-market or employer data relevant to entry routes before showing a recommendation.
Additional valid solution routes: 1) Interactive industry map: break entry routes into sectors, value-chain stages, employer types, job families and specialisations so the user can drill down. | 2) Personalised highlight: use the user's subjects, skills, interests and goals to highlight the parts of the industry most relevant to them. | 3) Evidence check: use current provider, vacancy, labour-market or employer data relevant to entry routes before showing a recommendation. | 4) Compare routes: let the user compare this industry with 1–2 alternatives on jobs, skills, pathways, work conditions, growth and location. | 5) Real-world validation: suggest an employer conversation, work experience, project, industry event or short learning activity to test whether the industry actually appeals.

DATA / EVIDENCE RULE
CURRENT EVIDENCE REQUIRED: do not present time-sensitive claims as current without approved live/read data. If unavailable, set status=NEEDS_RESEARCH and name the exact missing evidence.
Unknown is not the same as negative or missing capability. Separate user-confirmed facts, sourced facts and AI inference.

REQUIRED RESULT
Produce: Entry routes through school subjects, VET, university, apprenticeship, short learning and experience.
The result must explain why it matters, show meaningful alternatives or uncertainty where relevant, and avoid deterministic recommendations.

READINESS / SUCCESS CHECK
Name: Study / Pathway Readiness.
Dimensions: Goal clarity; Requirement evidence; Fit to constraints; Route feasibility; Backup/next-step readiness.
Meaning: A 0–100 readiness/completeness score for this decision step. It is not a probability of career, study, job or life success..
Proceed rule: Proceed at 75+ and no critical prerequisite, cost, eligibility or route dependency remains unknown. Otherwise research or build a Plan B..
Show the dimension breakdown and blockers. Do not present the score as likelihood of life/career success.

COMPLETION / STOP CONDITION
Stop when you can produce: Entry routes through school subjects, VET, university, apprenticeship, short learning and experience. Do not continue asking questions once the output is materially supported. Apply the readiness rule: Proceed at 75+ and no critical prerequisite, cost, eligibility or route dependency remains unknown. Otherwise research or build a Plan B. If a critical fact is unavailable, stop with NEEDS_INPUT or NEEDS_RESEARCH instead of guessing.

PROCEED
If the proceed rule is met, let the user continue with: Subjects for This Industry. Otherwise show exactly what is missing and offer one small next step instead of forcing a decision.
Primary next action: Subjects for This Industry.
Next related prompts: Subjects for This Industry; Qualifications Used.

save_policy=SESSION_ONLY. No automatic profile update is defined.
Never silently save AI-inferred traits, preferences, capability or fit.

Return a compact result to Oala containing: confirmed user inputs, result, evidence/unknowns, Study / Pathway Readiness, and recommended next action. Do not send click-by-click interaction history.

Map qualifications to major job families without implying everyone needs the same credential.

CATEGORY: Industry Intelligence > Industry work reality
OBJECTIVE TYPE: UNDERSTAND
INTERACTION MODE: HYBRID
RISK: LEVEL_0 (analysis/discovery)

PURPOSE
Separate industry median/context from occupation, career stage and location-specific earnings.

SERVE WHEN
Serve when user confuses industry average with occupation pay. Use known context first; ask only for missing information that changes the result.

DO NOT SERVE WHEN

USER EXPERIENCE TARGET
Start state: interested in a field but lacking a detailed picture of how the industry works
Afterward the user should feel: oriented, informed, and able to connect sectors, employers, roles, skills and trends.

Experience principle: Focused cards with progressive disclosure: one useful choice at a time, then a concise result and next action. Generation mode: HYBRID.

INPUT CONTRACT
Use known context first. Relevant inputs: Industry employment/workforce data, occupation mix, region and user preferences.
Do not re-ask known information. If something material is missing, ask only the single highest-impact missing item first.

INTERACTION CONTRACT
Allowed primitives: entity_picker, evidence_panel, short_answer, action_handoff.

Name: Industry Understanding Readiness.

Stop when you can produce: Work environment, hours, geography, earnings context and workforce composition. Do not continue asking questions once the output is materially supported. save_policy=SESSION_ONLY. No automatic profile update is defined.

objectives.static_findings: An industry can grow while only some occupations are in shortage, and shortage indicators have different causes. Vacancy volume alone is not proof of a worker shortage.
objectives.recommended_patch: Never label an entire industry SHORTAGE from one vacancy or broad growth signal. Distinguish shortage evidence from recruitment difficulty, high vacancy volume and projected demand. Record geography and period. Where available, classify likely driver as INSUFFICIENT_SUPPLY, LOCATION_MISMATCH, EXPERIENCE_GAP, CREDENTIAL_BOTTLENECK, TRAINING_BOTTLENECK, RETENTION_OR_CONDITIONS, RAPID_GROWTH or UNKNOWN. Do not infer easy hiring, higher pay or guaranteed jobs for an individual from shortage status.

CATEGORY: Industry Intelligence > Industry risks
OBJECTIVE TYPE: DECIDE
INTERACTION MODE: HYBRID
RISK: LEVEL_0 (analysis/discovery)

PURPOSE
Explain sensitivity to economic cycles, public funding, contracts, commodity prices or recurring demand.

SERVE WHEN
Serve when user values job stability. Use known context first; ask only for missing information that changes the result.

DO NOT SERVE WHEN
Do not surface this objective when the user is asking for an unrelated task, when 'Cyclical or Stable?' is already resolved and no material context changed, or when another objective is clearly more specific. Do not use it merely to collect extra profile data.

USER EXPERIENCE TARGET
Start state: interested in a field but lacking a detailed picture of how the industry works
Afterward the user should feel: oriented, informed, and able to connect sectors, employers, roles, skills and trends.
Desired behaviour: explore the most relevant branches, compare industries, and identify where to go deeper.
Experience principle: Focused cards with progressive disclosure: one useful choice at a time, then a concise result and next action. Generation mode: HYBRID.

INPUT CONTRACT
Use known context first. Relevant inputs: Industry macro conditions, regulation, technology, funding, supply chain and demand evidence.
Do not re-ask known information. If something material is missing, ask only the single highest-impact missing item first.
Questions must be concrete, short and age-appropriate. Ask only one high-impact thing at a time. Prefer examples, forced choices, rankings or real scenarios over abstract self-ratings. Offer Unsure/Not applicable when appropriate. Never imply that one answer determines a career, course or identity.

INTERACTION CONTRACT
Allowed primitives: entity_picker, ranking, tradeoff_matrix, readiness_scorecard, short_answer, action_handoff.
Preferred flow: ranking -> tradeoff_matrix -> readiness_scorecard -> action_handoff.
Maximum interactive components/questions before synthesis: 6.
Do not invent a new component type. Do not generate HTML.

STRATEGY
Choose the lightest method that can resolve the objective. Preferred solution patterns: Interactive industry map: break cyclical or stable? into sectors, value-chain stages, employer types, job families and specialisations so the user can drill down. | Personalised highlight: use the user's subjects, skills, interests and goals to highlight the parts of the industry most relevant to them. | Evidence check: use current provider, vacancy, labour-market or employer data relevant to cyclical or stable? before showing a recommendation.

Name: Industry Understanding Readiness.

Stop when you can produce: Risk factors and stability/cyclicality context. Do not continue asking questions once the output is materially supported. TOPIC: Would I Like This Industry?
CATEGORY: Industry Intelligence > Industry fit
OBJECTIVE TYPE: ASSESS
INTERACTION MODE: HYBRID
RISK: LEVEL_0 (analysis/discovery)

PURPOSE
Compare interests, values, skills, environment, location, study tolerance, salary expectations and goals.

SERVE WHEN
Serve when user wants person-industry fit. Use known context first; ask only for missing information that changes the result.

DO NOT SERVE WHEN
Do not surface this objective when the user is asking for an unrelated task, when 'Would I Like This Industry?' is already resolved and no material context changed, or when another objective is clearly more specific. Do not use it merely to collect extra profile data.

USER EXPERIENCE TARGET
Start state: interested in a field but lacking a detailed picture of how the industry works
Afterward the user should feel: oriented, informed, and able to connect sectors, employers, roles, skills and trends.
Desired behaviour: explore the most relevant branches, compare industries, and identify where to go deeper.
Experience principle: Focused cards with progressive disclosure: one useful choice at a time, then a concise result and next action. Generation mode: HYBRID.

INPUT CONTRACT
Use known context first. Relevant inputs: Industry profile plus user interests, work values, skills, environment preferences, location and study tolerance.
Do not re-ask known information. If something material is missing, ask only the single highest-impact missing item first.
Questions must be concrete, short and age-appropriate. Ask only one high-impact thing at a time. Prefer examples, forced choices, rankings or real scenarios over abstract self-ratings. Offer Unsure/Not applicable when appropriate. Never imply that one answer determines a career, course or identity.

INTERACTION CONTRACT
Allowed primitives: entity_picker, pathway_builder, scenario_test, evidence_panel, readiness_scorecard, short_answer, action_handoff.
Preferred flow: evidence_panel -> readiness_scorecard -> entity_picker -> action_handoff.
Maximum interactive components/questions before synthesis: 6.
Do not invent a new component type. Do not generate HTML.

STRATEGY
Choose the lightest method that can resolve the objective. Preferred solution patterns: Profile-to-target match: compare the user's explicit interests, skills, constraints and evidence with the requirements behind would i like this industry?. | Strengths and friction view: show both likely matches and possible mismatches instead of a single fit score. | Evidence-based check: distinguish demonstrated evidence, self-reported capability, missing information and genuine gaps before making a fit judgement.
Additional valid solution routes: 1) Profile-to-target match: compare the user's explicit interests, skills, constraints and evidence with the requirements behind would i like this industry?. | 2) Strengths and friction view: show both likely matches and possible mismatches instead of a single fit score. | 3) Evidence-based check: distinguish demonstrated evidence, self-reported capability, missing information and genuine gaps before making a fit judgement. | 4) Evidence-on-demand: start from the user profile, then fetch current external data for would i like this industry? when it could change the answer. | 5) Try-before-deciding: suggest a low-risk validation step such as a project, work sample, short course, conversation with someone in the field, or work experience.

OBJECTIVE MINI-PROMPT v1.0
ID: IND_FIT_003
TOPIC: What Might Not Fit Me?
CATEGORY: Industry Intelligence > Industry fit
OBJECTIVE TYPE: ASSESS
INTERACTION MODE: HYBRID
RISK: LEVEL_0 (analysis/discovery)

PURPOSE
Show possible conflicts in environment, location, study, regulation, work style or job availability.

SERVE WHEN
Serve when user needs disconfirming evidence. Use known context first; ask only for missing information that changes the result.

DO NOT SERVE WHEN
Do not surface this objective when the user is asking for an unrelated task, when 'What Might Not Fit Me?' is already resolved and no material context changed, or when another objective is clearly more specific. Do not use it merely to collect extra profile data.

USER EXPERIENCE TARGET
Start state: interested in a field but lacking a detailed picture of how the industry works
Afterward the user should feel: oriented, informed, and able to connect sectors, employers, roles, skills and trends.
Desired behaviour: explore the most relevant branches, compare industries, and identify where to go deeper.
Experience principle: Focused cards with progressive disclosure: one useful choice at a time, then a concise result and next action. Generation mode: HYBRID.

INPUT CONTRACT
Use known context first. Relevant inputs: Industry profile plus user interests, work values, skills, environment preferences, location and study tolerance.
Do not re-ask known information. If something material is missing, ask only the single highest-impact missing item first.
Questions must be concrete, short and age-appropriate. Ask only one high-impact thing at a time. Prefer examples, forced choices, rankings or real scenarios over abstract self-ratings. Offer Unsure/Not applicable when appropriate. Never imply that one answer determines a career, course or identity.

INTERACTION CONTRACT
Allowed primitives: entity_picker, pathway_builder, scenario_test, evidence_panel, readiness_scorecard, short_answer, action_handoff.
Preferred flow: evidence_panel -> readiness_scorecard -> entity_picker -> action_handoff.
Maximum interactive components/questions before synthesis: 6.
Do not invent a new component type. Do not generate HTML.

STRATEGY
Choose the lightest method that can resolve the objective. Preferred solution patterns: Profile-to-target match: compare the user's explicit interests, skills, constraints and evidence with the requirements behind what might not fit me?. | Strengths and friction view: show both likely matches and possible mismatches instead of a single fit score. | Evidence-based check: distinguish demonstrated evidence, self-reported capability, missing information and genuine gaps before making a fit judgement.
Additional valid solution routes: 1) Profile-to-target match: compare the user's explicit interests, skills, constraints and evidence with the requirements behind what might not fit me?. | 2) Strengths and friction view: show both likely matches and possible mismatches instead of a single fit score. | 3) Evidence-based check: distinguish demonstrated evidence, self-reported capability, missing information and genuine gaps before making a fit judgement. | 4) Evidence-on-demand: start from the user profile, then fetch current external data for what might not fit me? when it could change the answer. | 5) Try-before-deciding: suggest a low-risk validation step such as a project, work sample, short course, conversation with someone in the field, or work experience.

objectives.static_findings: Skill-use comparisons can become keyword counts. The same tool or skill name may be peripheral in one job and core in another, and self-reported capability is not automatically evidenced proficiency.

Do not count identical keywords as equal use. Keep tools separate from underlying capabilities. If proficiency is unknown, do not assume advanced match. Summarize where the user’s evidenced skills create useful starting leverage and where domain knowledge/credentials remain separate gaps.
